Each variant loads its own curated feed set: ~25 categories for geopolitical, ~20 for tech, ~18 for finance\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e8 live video streams\u003c/strong\u003e — Bloomberg, Sky News, Al Jazeera, Euronews, DW, France24, CNBC, Al Arabiya — with automatic live detection that scrapes YouTube channel pages every 5 minutes to find active streams\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDesktop embed bridge\u003c/strong\u003e — YouTube's IFrame API restricts playback in native webviews (error 153). The dashboard detects this and transparently routes through a cloud-hosted embed proxy with bidirectional message passing (play/pause/mute/unmute/loadVideo)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eIdle-aware playback\u003c/strong\u003e — video players pause and are removed from the DOM after 5 minutes of inactivity, resuming when the user returns. Tab visibility changes also suspend/resume streams\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGlobal streaming quality control\u003c/strong\u003e — a user-selectable quality setting (auto, 360p, 480p, 720p) that applies to all live video streams across the dashboard. The preference persists in localStorage and propagates to active players via a \u003ccode\u003estream-quality-changed\u003c/code\u003e CustomEvent — no reload required when switching quality\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e19 live webcams\u003c/strong\u003e — real-time YouTube streams from geopolitical hotspots across 4 regions (Middle East, Europe, Americas, Asia-Pacific). Grid view shows 4 strategic feeds simultaneously; single-feed view available. Region filtering (ALL/MIDEAST/EUROPE/AMERICAS/ASIA), idle-aware playback that pauses after 5 minutes, and Intersection Observer-based lazy loading\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCustom keyword monitors\u003c/strong\u003e — user-defined keyword alerts with word-boundary matching (prevents \"ai\" from matching \"train\"), automatic color-coding from a 10-color palette, and multi-keyword support (comma-separated). Monitors search across both headline titles and descriptions and show real-time match counts\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEntity extraction\u003c/strong\u003e — Auto-links countries, leaders, organizations\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eInstant flat render\u003c/strong\u003e — news items appear immediately as a flat list the moment feed data arrives. ML-based clustering (topic grouping, entity extraction, sentiment analysis) runs asynchronously in the background and progressively upgrades the view when ready — eliminating the 1–3 second blank delay that would occur if clustering blocked initial render. Finance variant categories fetch with 5 concurrent requests (vs 3) for ~10–15 second faster cold starts\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eVirtual scrolling\u003c/strong\u003e — news panels with 15+ items use a custom virtual list renderer that only creates DOM elements for visible items plus a 3-item overscan buffer. Viewport spacers simulate full-list height. Uses \u003ccode\u003erequestAnimationFrame\u003c/code\u003e-batched scroll handling and \u003ccode\u003eResizeObserver\u003c/code\u003e for responsive adaptation. DOM elements are pooled and recycled rather than created/destroyed\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eSignal Aggregation \u0026amp; Anomaly Detection\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-signal-aggregation--anomaly-detection\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Signal Aggregation \u0026amp; Anomaly Detection\" href=\"#signal-aggregation--anomaly-detection\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMulti-source signal fusion\u003c/strong\u003e — internet outages, military flights, naval vessels, protests, AIS disruptions, satellite fires, and keyword spikes are aggregated into a unified intelligence picture with per-country and per-region clustering\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTemporal baseline anomaly detection\u003c/strong\u003e — Welford's online algorithm computes streaming mean/variance per event type, region, weekday, and month over a 90-day window. Bot detection uses a user-agent regex for 10+ known social crawler signatures\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eDesktop Application (Tauri)\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-desktop-application-tauri\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Desktop Application (Tauri)\" href=\"#desktop-application-tauri\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNative desktop app\u003c/strong\u003e for macOS, Windows, and Linux — packages the full dashboard with a local Node.js sidecar that runs all 60+ API handlers locally\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOS keychain integration\u003c/strong\u003e — API keys stored in the system credential manager (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager), never in plaintext files\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eToken-authenticated sidecar\u003c/strong\u003e — a unique session token prevents other local processes from accessing the sidecar on localhost. Generated per launch using randomized hashing\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCloud fallback\u003c/strong\u003e — when a local API handler fails or is missing, requests transparently fall through to the cloud deployment (worldmonitor.app) with origin headers stripped\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSettings window\u003c/strong\u003e — dedicated configuration UI (Cmd+,) with three tabs: \u003cstrong\u003eLLMs\u003c/strong\u003e (Ollama endpoint, model selection, Groq, OpenRouter), \u003cstrong\u003eAPI Keys\u003c/strong\u003e (12+ data source credentials with per-key validation), and \u003cstrong\u003eDebug \u0026amp; Logs\u003c/strong\u003e (traffic log, verbose mode, log files). Each tab runs an independent verification pipeline — saving in the LLMs tab doesn't block API Keys validation\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAutomatic model discovery\u003c/strong\u003e — when you set an Ollama or LM Studio endpoint URL in the LLMs tab, the settings panel immediately queries it for available models (tries Ollama native \u003ccode\u003e/api/tags\u003c/code\u003e first, then OpenAI-compatible \u003ccode\u003e/v1/models\u003c/code\u003e) and populates a dropdown. Embedding models are filtered out. If discovery fails, a manual text input appears as fallback\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCross-window secret sync\u003c/strong\u003e — the main dashboard and settings window run in separate webviews with independent JS contexts. Saving a secret in Settings writes to the OS keychain and broadcasts a \u003ccode\u003elocalStorage\u003c/code\u003e change event. The main window listens for this event and hot-reloads all secrets without requiring an app restart\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eConsolidated keychain vault\u003c/strong\u003e — all secrets are stored as a single JSON blob in one keychain entry (\u003ccode\u003esecrets-vault\u003c/code\u003e) rather than individual entries per key. This reduces macOS Keychain authorization prompts from 20+ to exactly 1 on each app launch. A one-time migration reads any existing individual entries, consolidates them, and cleans up the old format\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eVerbose debug mode\u003c/strong\u003e — toggle traffic logging with persistent state across restarts. View the last 200 requests with timing, status codes, and error details\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDevTools toggle\u003c/strong\u003e — Cmd+Alt+I opens the embedded web inspector for debugging\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAuto-update checker\u003c/strong\u003e — polls the cloud API for new versions every 6 hours. Displays a non-intrusive update badge with direct download link and per-version dismiss. Variant-aware — a Tech Monitor desktop app links to the correct Tech Monitor release asset\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eProgressive Web App\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-progressive-web-app\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Progressive Web App\" href=\"#progressive-web-app\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eInstallable\u003c/strong\u003e — the dashboard can be installed to the home screen on mobile or as a standalone desktop app via Chrome's install prompt. Full-screen \u003ccode\u003estandalone\u003c/code\u003e display mode with custom theme color\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOffline map support\u003c/strong\u003e — MapTiler tiles are cached using a CacheFirst strategy (up to 500 tiles, 30-day TTL), enabling map browsing without a network connection\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSmart caching strategies\u003c/strong\u003e — APIs and RSS feeds use NetworkOnly (real-time data must always be fresh), while fonts (1-year TTL), images (7-day StaleWhileRevalidate), and static assets (1-year immutable) are aggressively cached\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAuto-updating service worker\u003c/strong\u003e — checks for new versions every 60 minutes. Tauri desktop builds skip service worker registration entirely (uses native APIs instead)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOffline fallback\u003c/strong\u003e — a branded fallback page with retry button is served when the network is unavailable\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eAdditional Capabilities\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-additional-capabilities\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Additional Capabilities\" href=\"#additional-capabilities\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eSignal intelligence with \"Why It Matters\" context\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eInfrastructure cascade analysis with proximity correlation\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eMaritime \u0026amp; aviation tracking with surge detection\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ePrediction market integration (Polymarket) with 3-tier JA3 bypass (browser-direct → Tauri native TLS → cloud proxy)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eService status monitoring (cloud providers, AI services)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eShareable map state via URL parameters (view, zoom, coordinates, time range, active layers)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eData freshness monitoring across 16 data sources with explicit intelligence gap reporting\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ePer-feed circuit breakers with 5-minute cooldowns to prevent cascading failures\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBrowser-side ML worker\u003c/strong\u003e (Transformers.js) for NER and sentiment analysis without server dependency — controllable via a \"Browser Local Model\" toggle in AI Flow settings. When disabled, the ML worker is never initialized, eliminating ONNX model downloads and WebGL memory allocation. The toggle propagates dynamically — enabling it mid-session initializes the worker immediately, disabling it terminates it\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCmd+K command palette\u003c/strong\u003e — fuzzy search across 20+ result types (news, countries, hotspots, markets, bases, cables, datacenters, nuclear facilities, and more), plus layer toggle commands, layer presets (e.g., \u003ccode\u003elayers:military\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003elayers:finance\u003c/code\u003e), and instant country brief navigation for all ~250 ISO countries with flag emoji icons. Curated countries include search aliases (e.g., typing \"kremlin\" or \"putin\" finds Russia). Scoring ranks exact matches (3pts) above prefix matches (2pts) above substring matches (1pt). Recent searches are stored in localStorage (max 8 entries)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHistorical playback\u003c/strong\u003e — dashboard snapshots are stored in IndexedDB. A time slider allows rewinding to any saved state, with live updates paused during playback\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMobile detection\u003c/strong\u003e — screens below 768px receive a warning modal since the dashboard is designed for multi-panel desktop use\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUCDP conflict classification\u003c/strong\u003e — countries with active wars (1,000+ battle deaths/year) receive automatic CII floor scores, preventing optimistic drift. The UCDP GED API integration uses automatic version discovery (probing multiple year-based API versions in parallel), negative caching (5-minute backoff after upstream failures), discovered-version caching (1-hour TTL), and stale-on-error fallback to ensure conflict data is always available even when the upstream API is intermittently down\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHAPI humanitarian data\u003c/strong\u003e — UN OCHA humanitarian access metrics and displacement flows feed into country-level instability scoring with dual-perspective (origins vs. hosts) panel\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eIdle-aware resource management\u003c/strong\u003e — animations pause after 2 minutes of inactivity and when the tab is hidden, preventing battery drain. Video streams are destroyed from the DOM and recreated on return\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCountry-specific stock indices\u003c/strong\u003e — country briefs display the primary stock market index with 1-week change (S\u0026amp;P 500 for US, Shanghai Composite for China, etc.) via the \u003ccode\u003e/api/stock-index\u003c/code\u003e endpoint\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eClimate anomaly panel\u003c/strong\u003e — 15 conflict-prone zones monitored for temperature/precipitation deviations against 30-day ERA5 baselines, with severity classification feeding into CII\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCountry brief export\u003c/strong\u003e — every brief is downloadable as structured JSON, flattened CSV, or rendered PNG image, enabling offline analysis and reporting workflows\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePrint/PDF support\u003c/strong\u003e — country briefs include a print button that triggers the browser's native print dialog, producing clean PDF output\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOil \u0026amp; energy analytics\u003c/strong\u003e — WTI/Brent crude prices, US production (Mbbl/d), and inventory levels via the EIA API with weekly trend detection\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePopulation exposure estimation\u003c/strong\u003e — WorldPop density data estimates civilian population within event-specific radii (50–100km) for conflicts, earthquakes, floods, and wildfires\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTrending keywords panel\u003c/strong\u003e — real-time display of surging terms across all RSS feeds with spike severity, source count, and AI-generated context summaries\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDownload banner\u003c/strong\u003e — persistent notification for web users linking to native desktop installers for their detected platform\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDownload API\u003c/strong\u003e — \u003ccode\u003e/api/download?platform={windows-exe|windows-msi|macos-arm64|macos-x64|linux-appimage}[\u0026amp;variant={full|tech|finance}]\u003c/code\u003e redirects to the matching GitHub Release asset, with fallback to the releases page\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUniversal country coverage\u003c/strong\u003e — every country with incoming event data receives a live CII score automatically, not just the 23 curated tier-1 nations. Clicking any country opens a full brief with available data (news, markets, infrastructure), and non-curated countries use sensible default baselines (\u003ccode\u003eDEFAULT_BASELINE_RISK = 15\u003c/code\u003e) with display names resolved via \u003ccode\u003eIntl.DisplayNames\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFeature toggles\u003c/strong\u003e — 15 runtime toggles (AI/Ollama, AI/Groq, AI/OpenRouter, FRED economic, EIA energy, internet outages, ACLED conflicts, threat intel feeds, AIS relay, OpenSky, Finnhub, NASA FIRMS) stored in \u003ccode\u003elocalStorage\u003c/code\u003e, allowing administrators to enable/disable data sources without rebuilding\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAIS chokepoint detection\u003c/strong\u003e — the relay server monitors 8 strategic maritime chokepoints (Strait of Hormuz, Suez Canal, Malacca Strait, Bab el-Mandeb, Panama Canal, Taiwan Strait, South China Sea, Turkish Straits) and classifies transiting vessels by naval candidacy using MMSI prefixes, ship type codes, and name patterns\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAIS density grid\u003c/strong\u003e — vessel positions are aggregated into 2°×2° geographic cells over 30-minute windows, producing a heatmap of maritime traffic density that feeds into convergence detection\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePanel resizing\u003c/strong\u003e — drag handles on panel edges allow height adjustment (span-1 through span-4 grid rows), persisted to localStorage. Double-click resets to default height\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUltra-wide monitor layout\u003c/strong\u003e — on screens 2000px+ wide, the layout automatically switches from vertical stacking to an L-shaped arrangement: the map floats left at 60% width while panels tile to the right and below it, maximizing screen real estate on ultra-wide and 4K monitors. Uses CSS \u003ccode\u003edisplay: contents\u003c/code\u003e and float-based wrapping — no JavaScript layout engine required\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDark/light theme\u003c/strong\u003e — persistent theme toggle with 20+ semantic color variable overrides. Dark theme is the default. Theme preference is stored in localStorage, applied before first paint (no flash of wrong theme), and syncs the \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;meta name=\"theme-color\"\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e for native browser chrome. A \u003ccode\u003etheme-changed\u003c/code\u003e custom event allows panels to react to switches\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePanel drag-and-drop reordering\u003c/strong\u003e — panels can be reordered via drag-and-drop within the grid. The custom order is persisted to localStorage and restored on reload. Touch events are supported for tablet use\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMap pin mode\u003c/strong\u003e — a 📌 button pins the map in a fixed position so it remains visible while scrolling through panels. Pin state is persisted to localStorage\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOpt-in intelligence alert popups\u003c/strong\u003e — the Intelligence Findings badge accumulates signals and alerts silently in the background. A toggle switch in the badge's dropdown header lets users opt in to automatic popup notifications when high-priority findings arrive. The popup preference is stored in localStorage (default: off), so the dashboard never interrupts users who haven't explicitly requested it. The badge continues counting and pulsing regardless of the popup setting — clicking the badge always opens the full findings dropdown\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003chr\u003e\n\u003cdiv The brief is organized into a two-column layout:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLeft column\u003c/strong\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eInstability Index\u003c/strong\u003e — animated SVG score ring (0–100) with four component breakdown bars (Unrest, Conflict, Security, Information), severity badge, and trend indicator\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eIntelligence Brief\u003c/strong\u003e — AI-generated analysis (Ollama local / Groq / OpenRouter, depending on configured provider) with inline citation anchors \u003ccode\u003e[1]\u003c/code\u003e–\u003ccode\u003e[8]\u003c/code\u003e that scroll to the corresponding news source when clicked\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTop News\u003c/strong\u003e — 8 most relevant headlines for the country, threat-level color-coded, with source and time-ago metadata\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRight column\u003c/strong\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eActive Signals\u003c/strong\u003e — real-time chip indicators for protests, military aircraft, naval vessels, internet outages, earthquakes, displacement flows, climate stress, conflict events, and the country's stock market index (1-week change)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e7-Day Timeline\u003c/strong\u003e — D3.js-rendered event chart with 4 severity-coded lanes (protest, conflict, natural, military), interactive tooltips, and responsive resizing\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePrediction Markets\u003c/strong\u003e — top 3 Polymarket contracts by volume with probability bars and external links\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eInfrastructure Exposure\u003c/strong\u003e — pipelines, undersea cables, datacenters, military bases, nuclear facilities, and ports within a 600km radius of the country centroid, ranked by distance\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHeadline relevance filtering\u003c/strong\u003e: each country has an alias map (e.g., \u003ccode\u003eUS → [\"united states\", \"american\", \"washington\", \"pentagon\", \"biden\", \"trump\"]\u003c/code\u003e). Headlines are filtered using a negative-match algorithm — if another country's alias appears earlier in the headline title than the target country's alias, the headline is excluded. This prevents cross-contamination (e.g., a headline about Venezuela mentioning \"Washington sanctions\" appearing in the US brief).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExport options\u003c/strong\u003e: briefs are exportable as JSON (structured data with all scores, signals, and headlines), CSV (flattened tabular format), or PNG image. A print button triggers the browser's native print dialog for PDF export.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eLocal-First Country Detection\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-local-first-country-detection\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Local-First Country Detection\" href=\"#local-first-country-detection\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMap clicks resolve to countries using a local geometry service rather than relying on network reverse-geocoding (Nominatim). The system loads a GeoJSON file containing polygon boundaries for ~200 countries and builds an indexed spatial lookup:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBounding box pre-filter\u003c/strong\u003e — each country's polygon(s) are wrapped in a bounding box (\u003ccode\u003e[minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat]\u003c/code\u003e). Points outside the bbox are rejected without polygon intersection testing.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRay-casting algorithm\u003c/strong\u003e — for points inside the bbox, a ray is cast from the point along the positive x-axis. The number of polygon edge intersections determines inside/outside status (odd = inside). Edge cases are handled: points on segment boundaries return \u003ccode\u003etrue\u003c/code\u003e, and polygon holes are subtracted (a point inside an outer ring but also inside a hole is excluded).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMultiPolygon support\u003c/strong\u003e — countries with non-contiguous territories (e.g., the US with Alaska and Hawaii, Indonesia with thousands of islands) use MultiPolygon geometries where each polygon is tested independently.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis approach provides sub-millisecond country detection entirely in the browser, with no network latency. The geometry data is preloaded at app startup and cached for the session. For countries not in the GeoJSON (rare), the system falls back to hardcoded rectangular bounding boxes, and finally to network reverse-geocoding as a last resort.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHeadline deduplication\u003c/strong\u003e — before sending to any LLM, headlines are compared pairwise using word-overlap similarity. Near-duplicates (\u0026gt;60% overlap) are merged, reducing the prompt by 20–40% and preventing the LLM from wasting tokens on repeated stories\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eVariant-aware prompting\u003c/strong\u003e — the system prompt adapts to the active dashboard variant. Geopolitical summaries emphasize conflict escalation and diplomatic shifts; tech summaries focus on funding rounds and AI breakthroughs; finance summaries highlight market movements and central bank signals\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLanguage-aware output\u003c/strong\u003e — when the UI language is non-English, the prompt instructs the LLM to generate the summary in that language\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRedis deduplication\u003c/strong\u003e — summaries are cached with a composite key (\u003ccode\u003esummary:v3:{mode}:{variant}:{lang}:{hash}\u003c/code\u003e) so the same headlines viewed by 1,000 concurrent users trigger exactly one LLM call. Cache TTL is 24 hours\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGraceful fallback\u003c/strong\u003e — if a provider returns \u003ccode\u003e{fallback: true}\u003c/code\u003e (missing API key or endpoint unreachable), the chain silently advances to the next tier. Progress callbacks update the UI to show which provider is being attempted\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe Ollama tier communicates via the OpenAI-compatible \u003ccode\u003e/v1/chat/completions\u003c/code\u003e endpoint, making it compatible with any local inference server that implements this standard (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp server, vLLM, etc.).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eThreat Classification Pipeline\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca classification pipeline:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eKeyword classifier\u003c/strong\u003e (instant, \u003ccode\u003esource: 'keyword'\u003c/code\u003e) — pattern-matches against ~120 threat keywords organized by severity tier (critical → high → medium → low → info) and 14 event categories (conflict, protest, disaster, diplomatic, economic, terrorism, cyber, health, environmental, military, crime, infrastructure, tech, general). Keywords use word-boundary regex matching to prevent false positives (e.g., \"war\" won't match \"award\"). Each match returns a severity level, category, and confidence score. Variant-specific keyword sets ensure the tech variant doesn't flag \"sanctions\" in non-geopolitical contexts.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBrowser-side ML\u003c/strong\u003e (async, \u003ccode\u003esource: 'ml'\u003c/code\u003e) — Transformers.js runs NER, sentiment analysis, and topic classification directly in the browser with no server dependency. Provides a second classification opinion without any API call.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLLM classifier\u003c/strong\u003e (batched async, \u003ccode\u003esource: 'llm'\u003c/code\u003e) — headlines are collected into a batch queue and fired as parallel \u003ccode\u003eclassifyEvent\u003c/code\u003e RPCs via the sebuf proto client. Each RPC calls the configured LLM provider (Groq Llama 3.1 8B at temperature 0, or Ollama for local inference). Results are cached in Redis (24h TTL) keyed by headline hash. When 500-series errors occur, the LLM classifier automatically pauses its queue to avoid wasting API quota, resuming after an exponential backoff delay. When the LLM result arrives, it overrides the keyword result only if its confidence is higher.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis hybrid approach means the UI is never blocked waiting for AI — users see keyword results instantly, with ML and LLM refinements arriving within seconds and persisting for all subsequent visitors. Each classification carries its \u003ccode\u003esource\u003c/code\u003e tag (\u003ccode\u003ekeyword\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eml\u003c/code\u003e, or \u003ccode\u003ellm\u003c/code\u003e) so downstream consumers can weight confidence accordingly.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eCountry Instability Index (CII)\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-country-instability-index-cii\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Country Instability Index (CII)\" href=\"#country-instability-index-cii\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEvery country with incoming event data receives a live instability score (0–100). 23 curated tier-1 nations (US, Russia, China, Ukraine, Iran, Israel, Taiwan, North Korea, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Poland, Germany, France, UK, India, Pakistan, Syria, Yemen, Myanmar, Venezuela, Brazil, UAE, and Japan) have individually tuned baseline risk profiles and keyword lists. Western Pacific, Horn of Africa) with 38+ associated military bases. It classifies vessel clusters near hotspots by activity type:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDeployment\u003c/strong\u003e — carrier present with 5+ vessels\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExercise\u003c/strong\u003e — combatants present in formation\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTransit\u003c/strong\u003e — vessels passing through\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eForeign military presence is dual-credited: the operator's country is flagged for force projection, and the host location's country is flagged for foreign military threat. AIS gaps (dark ships) are flagged as potential signal discipline indicators.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eUSNI Fleet Intelligence\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-usni-fleet-intelligence\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: USNI Fleet Intelligence\" href=\"#usni-fleet-intelligence\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe dashboard ingests weekly U.S. Naval Institute (USNI) fleet deployment reports and merges them with live AIS vessel tracking data. Each report is parsed for carrier strike groups, amphibious ready groups, and individual combatant deployments — extracting hull numbers, vessel names, operational regions, and mission notes.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe merge algorithm matches USNI entries against live AIS-tracked vessels by hull number and normalized name. Matched vessels receive enrichment: strike group assignment, deployment status (deployed / returning / in-port), and operational theater. Unmatched USNI entries (submarines, vessels running dark) generate synthetic positions based on the last known operational region, with coordinate scattering to prevent marker overlap.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis dual-source approach provides a more complete operational picture than either AIS or USNI alone — AIS reveals real-time positions but misses submarines and vessels with transponders off, while USNI captures the complete order of battle but with weekly lag.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eAircraft Enrichment\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-aircraft-enrichment\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Aircraft Enrichment\" href=\"#aircraft-enrichment\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMilitary flights detected via ADS-B transponder data are enriched through the Wingbits aviation intelligence API, which provides aircraft registration, manufacturer, model, owner, and operator details. Each flight receives a military confidence classification:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eConfidence\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eCriteria\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eConfirmed\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eOperator matches a known military branch or defense contractor\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLikely\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAircraft type is exclusively military (tanker, AWACS, fighter)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePossible\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eGovernment-registered aircraft in a military operating area\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCivilian\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eNo military indicators detected\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEnrichment queries are batched (up to 50 aircraft per request) and cached with a circuit breaker pattern to avoid hammering the upstream API during high-traffic periods. The enriched metadata feeds into the Theater Posture Assessment — a KC-135 tanker paired with F-15s and an E-3 AWACS indicates strike packaging, not routine training.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eUndersea Cable Health Monitoring\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-undersea-cable-health-monitoring\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Undersea Cable Health Monitoring\" href=\"#undersea-cable-health-monitoring\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eBeyond displaying static cable routes on the map, the system actively monitors cable health by cross-referencing two live data sources:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNGA Navigational Warnings\u003c/strong\u003e — the U.S. National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency publishes maritime safety broadcasts that frequently mention cable repair operations. The system filters these warnings for cable-related keywords (\u003ccode\u003eCABLE\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eCABLESHIP\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eSUBMARINE CABLE\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eFIBER OPTIC\u003c/code\u003e, etc.) and extracts structured data: vessel names, DMS/decimal coordinates, advisory severity, and repair ETAs. Each warning is matched to the nearest cataloged undersea cable within a 5° geographic radius.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAIS Cable Ship Tracking\u003c/strong\u003e — dedicated cable repair vessels (CS Reliance, Île de Bréhat, Cable Innovator, etc.) are identified by name pattern matching against AIS transponder data. Ship status is classified as \u003ccode\u003eenroute\u003c/code\u003e (transiting to repair site) or \u003ccode\u003eon-station\u003c/code\u003e (actively working) based on keyword analysis of the warning text.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAdvisories are classified by severity: \u003ccode\u003efault\u003c/code\u003e (cable break, cut, or damage — potential traffic rerouting) or \u003ccode\u003edegraded\u003c/code\u003e (repair work in progress with partial capacity). Impact descriptions are generated dynamically, linking the advisory to the specific cable and the countries it serves — enabling questions like \"which cables serving South Asia are currently under repair?\"\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHealth scoring algorithm\u003c/strong\u003e — Each cable receives a composite health score (0–100) computed from weighted signals with exponential time decay:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"signal_weight = severity × (e^(-λ × age_hours))     where λ = ln(2) / 168 (7-day half-life)\nhealth_score  = max(0, 100 − Σ(signal_weights) × 100)\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003esignal_weight = severity × (e^(-λ × age_hours))     where λ = ln(2) / 168 (7-day half-life)\nhealth_score  = max(0, 100 − Σ(signal_weights) × 100)\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSignals are classified into two kinds: \u003ccode\u003eoperator_fault\u003c/code\u003e (confirmed cable damage — severity 1.0) and \u003ccode\u003ecable_advisory\u003c/code\u003e (repair operations, navigational warnings — severity 0.6). Geographic matching uses cosine-latitude-corrected equirectangular approximation to find the nearest cataloged cable within 50km of each NGA warning's coordinates. Results are cached in Redis (6-hour TTL for complete results, 10 minutes for partial) with an in-memory fallback that serves stale data when Redis is unavailable — ensuring the cable health layer never shows blank data even during cache failures.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eInfrastructure Cascade Modeling\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-infrastructure-cascade-modeling\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Infrastructure Cascade Modeling\" href=\"#infrastructure-cascade-modeling\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eBeyond proximity correlation, the system models how disruptions propagate through interconnected infrastructure. A dependency graph connects undersea cables, pipelines, ports, chokepoints, and countries with weighted edges representing capacity dependencies:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"Disruption Event → Affected Node → Cascade Propagation (BFS, depth ≤ 3)\n                                          │\n                    ┌─────────────────────┤\n                    ▼                     ▼\n            Direct Impact         Indirect Impact\n         (e.g., cable cut)    (countries served by cable)\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eDisruption Event → Affected Node → Cascade Propagation (BFS, depth ≤ 3)\n                                          │\n                    ┌─────────────────────┤\n                    ▼                     ▼\n            Direct Impact         Indirect Impact\n         (e.g., cable cut)    (countries served by cable)\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eImpact calculation\u003c/strong\u003e: \u003ccode\u003estrength = edge_weight × disruption_level × (1 − redundancy)\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eStrategic chokepoint modeling captures real-world dependencies:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStrait of Hormuz\u003c/strong\u003e — 80% of Japan's oil, 70% of South Korea's, 60% of India's, 40% of China's\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSuez Canal\u003c/strong\u003e — EU-Asia trade routes (Germany, Italy, UK, China)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMalacca Strait\u003c/strong\u003e — 80% of China's oil transit\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePorts are weighted by type: oil/LNG terminals (0.9 — critical), container ports (0.7), naval bases (0.4 — geopolitical but less economic). This enables questions like \"if the Strait of Hormuz closes, which countries face energy shortages within 30 days?\"\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eRelated Assets \u0026amp; Proximity Correlation\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-related-assets--proximity-correlation\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Related Assets \u0026amp; Proximity Correlation\" href=\"#related-assets--proximity-correlation\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhen a news event is geo-located, the system automatically identifies critical infrastructure within a 600km radius — pipelines, undersea cables, data centers, military bases, and nuclear facilities — ranked by distance. This enables instant geopolitical context: a cable cut near a strategic chokepoint, a protest near a nuclear facility, or troop movements near a data center cluster.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eNews Geo-Location\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-news-geo-location\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: News Geo-Location\" href=\"#news-geo-location\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA 74-hub strategic location database infers geography from headlines via keyword matching. Hubs span capitals, conflict zones, strategic chokepoints (Strait of Hormuz, Suez Canal, Malacca Strait), and international organizations. Confidence scoring is boosted for critical-tier hubs and active conflict zones, enabling map-driven news placement without requiring explicit location metadata from RSS feeds.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv prevent false positives (e.g., \"Iran\" matching \"Ukraine\"). Confidence scores are tiered by match quality: exact name matches score 1.0, aliases 0.85–0.95, and keyword matches 0.7. When the same entity surfaces across multiple independent data sources (news, military tracking, protest feeds, market signals), the system identifies it as a focal point and escalates its prominence in the intelligence picture.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eTemporal Baseline Anomaly Detection\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-temporal-baseline-anomaly-detection\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Temporal Baseline Anomaly Detection\" href=\"#temporal-baseline-anomaly-detection\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eRather than relying on static thresholds, the system learns what \"normal\" looks like and flags deviations. Each event type (military flights, naval vessels, protests, news velocity, AIS gaps, satellite fires) is tracked per region with separate baselines for each weekday and month — because military activity patterns differ on Tuesdays vs. weekends, and January vs. July.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe algorithm uses \u003cstrong\u003eWelford's online method\u003c/strong\u003e for numerically stable streaming computation of mean and variance, stored in Redis with a 90-day rolling window. When a new observation arrives, its z-score is computed against the learned baseline. Thresholds:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eZ-Score\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eSeverity\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eExample\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e≥ 1.5\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eLow\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eSlightly elevated protest activity\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e≥ 2.0\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eMedium\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eUnusual naval presence\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e≥ 3.0\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eHigh/Critical\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eMilitary flights 3x above baseline\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA minimum of 10 historical samples is required before anomalies are reported, preventing false positives during the learning phase. Anomalies are ingested back into the signal aggregator, where they compound with other signals for convergence detection.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eTrending Keyword Spike Detection\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-trending-keyword-spike-detection\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Trending Keyword Spike Detection\" href=\"#trending-keyword-spike-detection\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEvery RSS headline is tokenized into individual terms and tracked in per-term frequency maps. A 2-hour rolling window captures current activity while a 7-day baseline (refreshed hourly) establishes what \"normal\" looks like for each term. A spike fires when all conditions are met:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eCondition\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eThreshold\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAbsolute count\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u0026gt; \u003ccode\u003eminSpikeCount\u003c/code\u003e (5 mentions)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRelative surge\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u0026gt; baseline × \u003ccode\u003espikeMultiplier\u003c/code\u003e (3×)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSource diversity\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e≥ 2 unique RSS feed sources\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCooldown\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e30 minutes since last spike for the same term\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe tokenizer extracts CVE identifiers (\u003ccode\u003eCVE-2024-xxxxx\u003c/code\u003e), APT/FIN threat actor designators, and 12 compound terms for world leaders (e.g., \"Xi Jinping\", \"Kim Jong Un\") that would be lost by naive whitespace splitting. A configurable blocklist suppresses common noise terms.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eDetected spikes are auto-summarized via Groq (rate-limited to 5 summaries/hour) and emitted as \u003ccode\u003ekeyword_spike\u003c/code\u003e signals into the correlation engine, where they compound with other signal types for convergence detection. The term registry is capped at 10,000 entries with LRU eviction to bound memory usage. All thresholds (spike multiplier, min count, cooldown, blocked terms) are configurable via the Settings panel.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eProto-First API Contracts\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-proto-first-api-contracts\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Proto-First API Contracts\" href=\"#proto-first-api-contracts\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe entire API surface is defined in Protocol Buffer (\u003ccode\u003e.proto\u003c/code\u003e) files using \u003ca href=\"https://github.com/SebastienMelki/sebuf\"\u003esebuf\u003c/a\u003e HTTP annotations. Breaking changes are caught at CI time via \u003ccode\u003ebuf breaking\u003c/code\u003e against the main branch.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEdge gateway\u003c/strong\u003e — a single Vercel Edge Function (\u003ccode\u003eapi/[domain]/v1/[rpc].ts\u003c/code\u003e) imports all 20 \u003ccode\u003ecreateServiceRoutes()\u003c/code\u003e functions into a flat \u003ccode\u003eMap\u0026lt;string, handler\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e router. Every RPC is a POST endpoint at a static path (e.g., \u003ccode\u003ePOST /api/aviation/v1/list-airport-delays\u003c/code\u003e), with CORS enforcement, a top-level error boundary that hides internal details on 5xx responses, and rate-limit support (\u003ccode\u003eretryAfter\u003c/code\u003e on 429). Enrichment runs concurrently — 16 parallel lookups with a 12-second timeout, processing up to 250 IPs per collection run.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIOCs are classified into four types (\u003ccode\u003ec2_server\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003emalware_host\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ephishing\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003emalicious_url\u003c/code\u003e) with four severity levels, rendered as color-coded scatter dots on the globe. The layer uses a 10-minute cache, a 14-day rolling window, and caps display at 500 IOCs to maintain rendering performance.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" observation events\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e13 natural event categories (30-day open events)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eReal-time\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eGDACS events carry color-coded alert levels (Red = critical, Orange = high) and are filtered to exclude low-severity Green alerts. EONET wildfires are filtered to events within 48 hours to prevent stale data. Earthquakes from EONET are excluded since USGS provides higher-quality seismological data.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe merged output feeds into the signal aggregator for geographic convergence detection — e.g., an earthquake near a pipeline triggers an infrastructure cascade alert.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eDual-Source Protest Tracking\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-dual-source-protest-tracking\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Dual-Source Protest Tracking\" href=\"#dual-source-protest-tracking\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eProtest data is sourced from two independent providers to reduce single-source bias:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eACLED\u003c/strong\u003e (Armed Conflict Location \u0026amp; Event Data) — 30-day window, tokenized API with Redis caching (10-minute TTL). Covers protests, riots, strikes, and demonstrations with actor attribution and fatality counts.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGDELT\u003c/strong\u003e (Global Database of Events, Language, and Tone) — 7-day geospatial event feed filtered to protest keywords. Events with mention count ≥5 are included; those above 30 are marked as \u003ccode\u003evalidated\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEvents from both sources are \u003cstrong\u003eHaversine-deduplicated\u003c/strong\u003e on a 0.1° grid (~10km) with same-day matching. ACLED events take priority due to higher editorial confidence. Severity is classified as:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHigh\u003c/strong\u003e — fatalities present or riot/clash keywords\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMedium\u003c/strong\u003e — standard protest/demonstration\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLow\u003c/strong\u003e — default\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eProtest scoring is regime-aware: democratic countries use logarithmic scaling (routine protests don't trigger instability), while authoritarian states use linear scoring (every protest is significant). Fatalities and concurrent internet outages apply severity boosts.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eClimate Anomaly Detection\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-climate-anomaly-detection\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Climate Anomaly Detection\" href=\"#climate-anomaly-detection\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e15 conflict-prone and disaster-prone zones are continuously monitored for temperature and precipitation anomalies using Open-Meteo ERA5 reanalysis data. A 30-day baseline is computed, and current conditions are compared against it to determine severity:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eSeverity\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eTemperature Deviation\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003ePrecipitation Deviation\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExtreme\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u0026gt; 5°C above baseline\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u0026gt; 80mm/day above baseline\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eModerate\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u0026gt; 3°C above baseline\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u0026gt; 40mm/day above baseline\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNormal\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWithin expected range\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWithin expected range\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAnomalies feed into the signal aggregator, where they amplify CII scores for affected countries (climate stress is a recognized conflict accelerant). The Climate Anomaly panel surfaces these deviations in a severity-sorted list.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eDisplacement Tracking\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-displacement-tracking\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Displacement Tracking\" href=\"#displacement-tracking\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eRefugee and displacement data is sourced from the UN OCHA Humanitarian API (HAPI), providing population-level counts for refugees, asylum seekers, and internally displaced persons (IDPs). The Displacement panel offers two perspectives:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOrigins\u003c/strong\u003e — countries people are fleeing from, ranked by outflow volume\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHosts\u003c/strong\u003e — countries absorbing displaced populations, ranked by intake\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eCrisis badges flag countries with extreme displacement: \u0026gt; 1 million displaced (red), \u0026gt; 500,000 (orange). Displacement outflow feeds into the CII as a component signal — high displacement is a lagging indicator of instability that persists even when headlines move on.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003ePopulation Exposure Estimation\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-population-exposure-estimation\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Population Exposure Estimation\" href=\"#population-exposure-estimation\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eActive events (conflicts, earthquakes, floods, wildfires) are cross-referenced against WorldPop population density data to estimate the number of civilians within the impact zone. Event-specific radii reflect typical impact footprints:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eEvent Type\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eRadius\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eRationale\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eConflicts\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e50 km\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eDirect combat zone + displacement buffer\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEarthquakes\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e100 km\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eShaking intensity propagation\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFloods\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e100 km\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWatershed and drainage basin extent\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWildfires\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e30 km\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eSmoke and evacuation perimeter\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAPI calls to WorldPop are batched concurrently (max 10 parallel requests) to handle multiple simultaneous events without sequential bottlenecks. When a newer version is detected (semver comparison), a non-intrusive update badge appears with a direct link to the GitHub Release page.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eUpdate prompts are dismissable per-version — dismissing v2.5.0 won't suppress v2.6.0 notifications. The updater is variant-aware: a Tech Monitor desktop build links to the Tech Monitor release asset, not the full variant.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003e/api/version\u003c/code\u003e endpoint reads the latest GitHub Release tag and caches the result for 1 hour, so version checks don't hit the GitHub API on every request.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eTheme System\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-theme-system\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Theme System\" href=\"#theme-system\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe dashboard supports dark and light themes with a toggle in the header bar. Dark is the default, matching the OSINT/command-center aesthetic.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTheme state is stored in localStorage and applied via a \u003ccode\u003e[data-theme=\"light\"]\u003c/code\u003e attribute on the root element. Critically, the theme is applied before any components mount — an inline script in \u003ccode\u003eindex.html\u003c/code\u003e reads the preference and sets the attribute synchronously, preventing a flash of the wrong theme on load.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e20+ CSS custom properties are overridden in light mode to maintain contrast ratios: severity colors shift (e.g., \u003ccode\u003e--semantic-high\u003c/code\u003e changes from \u003ccode\u003e#ff8800\u003c/code\u003e to \u003ccode\u003e#ea580c\u003c/code\u003e), backgrounds lighten, and text inverts. Language-specific font stacks switch in \u003ccode\u003e:lang()\u003c/code\u003e selectors — Arabic uses Geeza Pro, Chinese uses PingFang SC.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTypography\u003c/strong\u003e — the dashboard uses a consolidated \u003ccode\u003e--font-mono\u003c/code\u003e CSS custom property that cascades through the entire UI: SF Mono → Monaco → Cascadia Code → Fira Code → DejaVu Sans Mono → Liberation Mono → system monospace. This single variable ensures typographic consistency across macOS (SF Mono/Monaco), Windows (Cascadia Code), and Linux (DejaVu Sans Mono/Liberation Mono). The settings window inherits the same variable, preventing font divergence between the main dashboard and configuration UI.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA \u003ccode\u003etheme-changed\u003c/code\u003e CustomEvent is dispatched on toggle, allowing panels with custom rendering (charts, maps, gauges) to re-render with the new palette.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003ePrivacy \u0026amp; Offline Architecture\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-privacy--offline-architecture\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Privacy \u0026amp; Offline Architecture\" href=\"#privacy--offline-architecture\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWorld Monitor is designed so that sensitive intelligence work can run entirely on local hardware with no data leaving the user's machine. The privacy architecture operates at three levels:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLevel 1 — Full Cloud (Web App)\u003c/strong\u003e\nAll processing happens server-side on Vercel Edge Functions. API keys are stored in Vercel environment variables. News feeds are proxied through domain-allowlisted endpoints. AI summaries use Groq or OpenRouter. This is the default for \u003ccode\u003eworldmonitor.app\u003c/code\u003e — convenient but cloud-dependent.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLevel 2 — Desktop with Cloud APIs (Tauri + Sidecar)\u003c/strong\u003e\nThe desktop app runs a local Node.js sidecar that mirrors all 60+ cloud API handlers. API keys are stored in the OS keychain (macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager), never in plaintext files. Requests are processed locally first; cloud is a transparent fallback for missing handlers. Credential management happens through a native settings window with per-key validation.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLevel 3 — Air-Gapped Local (Ollama + Desktop)\u003c/strong\u003e\nWith Ollama or LM Studio configured, AI summarization runs entirely on local hardware. Combined with the desktop sidecar, the core intelligence pipeline (news aggregation, threat classification, instability scoring, AI briefings) operates with zero cloud dependency. The browser-side ML pipeline (Transformers.js) provides NER, sentiment analysis, and fallback summarization without even a local server.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eCapability\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth
