patterns and improve the dashboard. The implementation enforces strict data safety at multiple levels:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTyped event allowlists\u003c/strong\u003e — every analytics event has a schema defining exactly which properties are permitted. Unlisted properties are silently dropped before transmission. This prevents accidental inclusion of sensitive data in analytics payloads, even if a developer passes extra fields.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAPI key stripping\u003c/strong\u003e — a \u003ccode\u003esanitize_properties\u003c/code\u003e callback runs on every outgoing event. Any string value matching common API key prefixes (\u003ccode\u003esk-\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003egsk_\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eor-\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eBearer \u003c/code\u003e) is replaced with \u003ccode\u003e[REDACTED]\u003c/code\u003e before it leaves the browser. This is defense-in-depth: even if a key somehow ends up in an event payload, it never reaches the analytics backend.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNo session recordings, no autocapture\u003c/strong\u003e — PostHog's session replay and automatic DOM event capture are explicitly disabled. Only explicitly instrumented events are tracked.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePseudonymous identity\u003c/strong\u003e — each installation generates a random UUID stored in localStorage. There is no user login, no email collection, and no cross-device tracking. The UUID is purely pseudonymous — it enables session attribution without identifying individuals.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAd-blocker bypass\u003c/strong\u003e — on the web, PostHog traffic is routed through a reverse proxy on the app's own domain (\u003ccode\u003e/ingest\u003c/code\u003e) rather than directly to PostHog's servers. This prevents ad blockers from silently dropping analytics requests, ensuring usage data is representative. Desktop builds use PostHog's direct endpoint since ad blockers aren't a factor in native apps.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOffline event queue\u003c/strong\u003e — the desktop app may launch without network connectivity. Events captured while offline are queued in localStorage (capped at 200 entries) and flushed to PostHog when connectivity is restored. A \u003ccode\u003ewindow.online\u003c/code\u003e listener triggers automatic flush on reconnection.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSuper properties\u003c/strong\u003e — every event automatically carries platform context: variant (world/tech/finance), app version, platform (web/desktop), screen dimensions, viewport size, device pixel ratio, browser language, and desktop OS/arch. This enables segmentation without per-event instrumentation.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e30+ typed events cover core user interactions: app load timing, panel views, LLM summary generation (provider, model, cache status), API key configuration snapshots, map layer toggles, variant switches, country brief opens, theme changes, language changes, search usage, panel resizing, webcam selections, and auto-update interactions.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAnalytics is entirely opt-out by omitting the \u003ccode\u003eVITE_POSTHOG_KEY\u003c/code\u003e environment variable. When the key is absent, all analytics functions are no-ops with zero runtime overhead.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eResponsive Layout System\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-responsive-layout-system\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Responsive Layout System\" href=\"#responsive-layout-system\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe dashboard adapts to four screen categories without JavaScript layout computation — all breakpoints are CSS-only:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eScreen Width\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eLayout\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eDetails\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u0026lt; 768px\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eMobile warning\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eModal recommends desktop; limited panel display with touch-optimized map popups\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e768px–2000px\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eStandard grid\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eVertical stack: map on top, panels in \u003ccode\u003eauto-fill\u003c/code\u003e grid (\u003ccode\u003eminmax(280px, 1fr)\u003c/code\u003e). Panels tile in rows that adapt to available width\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e2000px+\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eUltra-wide L-shape\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eMap floats left at 60% width, 65vh height. Panels wrap to the right of the map and below it using CSS \u003ccode\u003edisplay: contents\u003c/code\u003e on the grid container with \u003ccode\u003efloat: left\u003c/code\u003e on individual panels\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe ultra-wide layout is notable for its technique: \u003ccode\u003edisplay: contents\u003c/code\u003e dissolves the \u003ccode\u003e.panels-grid\u003c/code\u003e container so that individual panel elements become direct flow children of \u003ccode\u003e.main-content\u003c/code\u003e. Combined with \u003ccode\u003efloat: left\u003c/code\u003e on the map, this creates natural L-shaped content wrapping — panels fill the space to the right of the map, and when they overflow past the map's height, they spread to full width. No JavaScript layout engine is involved.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePanel heights are user-adjustable via drag handles (span-1 through span-4 grid rows), with layout state persisted to localStorage. Double-clicking a drag handle resets the panel to its default height.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eSignal Aggregation\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-signal-aggregation\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Signal Aggregation\" href=\"#signal-aggregation\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAll real-time data sources feed into a central signal aggregator that builds a unified geospatial intelligence picture. Signals are clustered by country and region, with each signal carrying a severity (low/medium/high), geographic coordinates, and metadata. The aggregator:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eClusters by country\u003c/strong\u003e — groups signals from diverse sources (flights, vessels, protests, fires, outages, \u003ccode\u003ekeyword_spike\u003c/code\u003e) into per-country profiles\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDetects regional convergence\u003c/strong\u003e — identifies when multiple signal types spike in the same geographic corridor (e.g., military flights + protests + satellite fires in Eastern Mediterranean)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFeeds downstream analysis\u003c/strong\u003e — the CII, hotspot escalation, focal point detection, and AI insights modules all consume the aggregated signal picture rather than raw data\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003ePizzINT Activity Monitor \u0026amp; GDELT Tension Index\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-pizzint-activity-monitor--gdelt-tension-index\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: PizzINT Activity Monitor \u0026amp; GDELT Tension Index\" href=\"#pizzint-activity-monitor--gdelt-tension-index\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe dashboard integrates two complementary geopolitical pulse indicators:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePizzINT DEFCON scoring\u003c/strong\u003e — monitors foot traffic patterns at key military, intelligence, and government locations worldwide via the PizzINT API. Aggregate activity levels across monitored sites are converted into a 5-level DEFCON-style readout:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eAdjusted Activity\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eDEFCON Level\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eLabel\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e≥ 85%\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e1\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eMaximum Activity\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e70% – 84%\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e2\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eHigh Activity\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e50% – 69%\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e3\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eElevated Activity\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e25% – 49%\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e4\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAbove Normal\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u0026lt; 25%\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e5\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eNormal Activity\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eActivity spikes at individual locations boost the aggregate score (+10 per spike, capped at 100). Data freshness is tracked per-location — the system distinguishes between stale readings (location sensor lag) and genuine low activity. Per-location detail includes current popularity percentage, spike magnitude, and open/closed status.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGDELT bilateral tension pairs\u003c/strong\u003e — six strategic country pairs (USA↔Russia, Russia↔Ukraine, USA↔China, China↔Taiwan, USA↔Iran, USA↔Venezuela) are tracked via GDELT's GPR (Goldstein Political Relations) batch API. Each pair shows a current tension score, a percentage change from the previous data point, and a trend direction (rising/stable/falling, with ±5% thresholds). Rising bilateral tension scores that coincide with military signal spikes in the same region feed into the focal point detection algorithm.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eData Freshness \u0026amp; Intelligence Gaps\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-data-freshness--intelligence-gaps\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Data Freshness \u0026amp; Intelligence Gaps\" href=\"#data-freshness--intelligence-gaps\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA singleton tracker monitors 24 data sources (GDELT, RSS, AIS, military flights, earthquakes, weather, outages, ACLED, Polymarket, economic indicators, NASA FIRMS, cyber threat feeds, trending keywords, oil/energy, population exposure, BIS central bank data, WTO trade policy, and more) with status categorization: fresh (\u0026lt;15 min), stale (1h), very_stale (6h), no_data, error, disabled. It explicitly reports \u003cstrong\u003eintelligence gaps\u003c/strong\u003e — what analysts can't see — preventing false confidence when critical data sources are down or degraded.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003ePrediction Markets as Leading Indicators\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-prediction-markets-as-leading-indicators\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Prediction Markets as Leading Indicators\" href=\"#prediction-markets-as-leading-indicators\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePolymarket geopolitical markets are queried using tag-based filters (Ukraine, Iran, China, Taiwan, etc.) with 5-minute caching. Market probability shifts are correlated with news volume: if a prediction market moves significantly before matching news arrives, this is flagged as a potential early-warning signal.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCloudflare JA3 bypass\u003c/strong\u003e — Polymarket's API is protected by Cloudflare TLS fingerprinting (JA3) that blocks all server-side requests. The system uses a 3-tier fallback:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eTier\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eMethod\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eWhen It Works\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e1\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eBrowser-direct fetch\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAlways (browser TLS passes Cloudflare)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e2\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eTauri native TLS (reqwest)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eDesktop app (Rust TLS fingerprint differs from Node.js)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e3\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eVercel edge proxy\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eRarely (edge runtime sometimes passes)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eOnce browser-direct succeeds, the system caches this state and skips fallback tiers on subsequent requests. Country-specific markets are fetched by mapping countries to Polymarket tags with name-variant matching (e.g., \"Russia\" matches titles containing \"Russian\", \"Moscow\", \"Kremlin\", \"Putin\").\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMarkets are filtered to exclude sports and entertainment (100+ exclusion keywords), require meaningful price divergence from 50% or volume above $50K, and are ranked by trading volume. Each dataset uses independent circuit breakers with 30-minute cache TTLs. BIS data freshness is tracked in the intelligence gap system — staleness or failures surface as explicit warnings rather than silent gaps.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eWTO Trade Policy Intelligence\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-wto-trade-policy-intelligence\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: WTO Trade Policy Intelligence\" href=\"#wto-trade-policy-intelligence\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe Trade Policy panel provides real-time visibility into global trade restrictions, tariffs, and barriers — critical for tracking economic warfare, sanctions impact, and supply chain disruption risk. Four data views are available:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eTab\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eData Source\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eContent\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRestrictions\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWTO trade monitoring\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eActive trade restrictions with imposing/affected countries, product categories, and enforcement dates\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTariffs\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWTO tariff database\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eTariff rate trends between country pairs (e.g., US↔China) with historical datapoints\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFlows\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWTO trade statistics\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eBilateral trade flow volumes with year-over-year change indicators\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBarriers\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWTO SPS/TBT notifications\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eSanitary, phytosanitary, and technical barriers to trade with status tracking\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003etrade/v1\u003c/code\u003e proto service defines four RPCs, each with its own circuit breaker (30-minute cache TTL) and \u003ccode\u003eupstreamUnavailable\u003c/code\u003e signaling for graceful degradation when WTO endpoints are temporarily unreachable. The panel is available on FULL and FINANCE variants. Trade policy data feeds into the data freshness tracker as \u003ccode\u003ewto_trade\u003c/code\u003e, with intelligence gap warnings when the WTO feed goes stale.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eSupply Chain Disruption Intelligence\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-supply-chain-disruption-intelligence\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Supply Chain Disruption Intelligence\" href=\"#supply-chain-disruption-intelligence\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe Supply Chain panel provides real-time visibility into global logistics risk across three complementary dimensions — strategic chokepoint health, shipping cost trends, and critical mineral concentration — enabling early detection of disruptions that cascade into economic and geopolitical consequences.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eChokepoints tab\u003c/strong\u003e — monitors 6 strategic maritime bottlenecks (Suez Canal, Strait of Malacca, Strait of Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb, Panama Canal, Taiwan Strait) by cross-referencing live navigational warnings with AIS vessel disruption data. Each chokepoint receives a disruption score (0–100) computed from warning severity and count, mapped to color-coded status indicators (green/yellow/red). Data is cached with a 5-minute TTL for near-real-time awareness.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eShipping Rates tab\u003c/strong\u003e — tracks two Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) series: the Deep Sea Freight Producer Price Index (\u003ccode\u003ePCU483111483111\u003c/code\u003e) and the Freight Transportation Services Index (\u003ccode\u003eTSIFRGHT\u003c/code\u003e). Statistical spike detection flags abnormal price movements against recent history. Inline SVG sparklines render 24 months of rate history at a glance. Cached for 1 hour to reflect the weekly release cadence of underlying data.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCritical Minerals tab\u003c/strong\u003e — applies the \u003cstrong\u003eHerfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI)\u003c/strong\u003e to 2024 global production data for minerals critical to technology and defense manufacturing — lithium, cobalt, rare earths, gallium, germanium, and others. The HHI quantifies supply concentration risk: a market dominated by a single producer scores near 10,000, while a perfectly distributed market scores near 0. Each mineral displays the top 3 producing countries with market share percentages, flagging single-country dependencies that represent strategic vulnerability (e.g., China's dominance in rare earth processing). This tab uses static production data, cached for 24 hours with no external API dependency.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe panel is available on the FULL (World Monitor) variant and integrates with the infrastructure cascade model — when a chokepoint disruption coincides with high mineral concentration risk for affected trade routes, the combined signal feeds into convergence detection.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eBTC ETF Flow Estimation\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-btc-etf-flow-estimation\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: BTC ETF Flow Estimation\" href=\"#btc-etf-flow-estimation\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTen spot Bitcoin ETFs are tracked via Yahoo Finance's 5-day chart API (IBIT, FBTC, ARKB, BITB, GBTC, HODL, BRRR, EZBC, BTCO, BTCW). Since ETF flow data requires expensive terminal subscriptions, the system estimates flow direction from publicly available signals:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePrice change\u003c/strong\u003e — daily close vs. previous close determines direction\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eVolume ratio\u003c/strong\u003e — current volume / trailing average volume measures conviction\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFlow magnitude\u003c/strong\u003e — \u003ccode\u003evolume × price × direction × 0.1\u003c/code\u003e provides a rough dollar estimate\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis is an approximation, not a substitute for official flow data, but it captures the direction and relative magnitude correctly. over perfection\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eKeyword classifier is instant; LLM refines asynchronously. Users never wait.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAssume failure\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003ePer-feed circuit breakers with 5-minute cooldowns. AI fallback chain: Ollama (local) → Groq → OpenRouter → browser-side T5. Redis cache failures degrade to in-memory fallback with stale-on-error. Negative caching (5-minute backoff after upstream failures) prevents hammering downed APIs. Every edge function returns stale cached data when upstream APIs are down. \u003cstrong\u003eCache stampede prevention\u003c/strong\u003e — \u003ccode\u003ecachedFetchJson\u003c/code\u003e uses an in-flight promise map to coalesce concurrent cache misses into a single upstream fetch: the first request creates and registers a Promise, all concurrent requests for the same key await that same Promise rather than independently hitting the upstream. Rate-sensitive APIs (Yahoo Finance) use staggered sequential requests with 150ms inter-request delays to avoid 429 throttling. UCDP conflict data uses automatic version discovery (probing multiple API versions in parallel), discovered-version caching (1-hour TTL), and stale-on-error fallback.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eShow what you can't see\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eIntelligence gap tracker explicitly reports data source outages rather than silently hiding them.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBrowser-first compute\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAnalysis (clustering, instability scoring, surge detection) runs client-side — no backend compute dependency for core intelligence.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLocal-first geolocation\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eCountry detection uses browser-side ray-casting against GeoJSON polygons rather than network reverse-geocoding. Sub-millisecond response, zero API dependency, works offline. Network geocoding is a fallback, not the primary path.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMulti-signal correlation\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eNo single data source is trusted alone. Focal points require convergence across news + military + markets + protests before escalating to critical.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGeopolitical grounding\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eHard-coded conflict zones, baseline country risk, and strategic chokepoints prevent statistical noise from generating false alerts in low-data regions.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDefense in depth\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eCORS origin allowlist, domain-allowlisted RSS proxy, server-side API key isolation, token-authenticated desktop sidecar, input sanitization with output encoding, IP rate limiting on AI endpoints.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCache everything, trust nothing\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThree-tier caching (in-memory → Redis → upstream) with versioned cache keys and stale-on-error fallback. Every API response includes \u003ccode\u003eX-Cache\u003c/code\u003e header for debugging. CDN layer (\u003ccode\u003es-maxage\u003c/code\u003e) absorbs repeated requests before they reach edge functions.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBandwidth efficiency\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eGzip compression on all relay responses (80% reduction). Content-hash static assets with 1-year immutable cache. Staggered polling intervals prevent synchronized API storms. Animations and polling pause on hidden tabs.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBaseline-aware alerting\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eTrending keyword detection uses rolling 2-hour windows against 7-day baselines with per-term spike multipliers, cooldowns, and source diversity requirements — surfacing genuine surges while suppressing noise.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eContract-first APIs\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eEvery API endpoint starts as a \u003ccode\u003e.proto\u003c/code\u003e definition with field validation, HTTP annotations, and examples. Code generation produces typed TypeScript clients and servers, eliminating schema drift. Breaking changes are caught automatically at CI time.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRun anywhere\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eSame codebase produces three specialized variants (geopolitical, tech, finance) and deploys to Vercel (web), Railway (relay), Tauri (desktop), and PWA (installable). Desktop sidecar mirrors all cloud API handlers locally. Service worker caches map tiles for offline use while keeping intelligence data always-fresh (NetworkOnly).\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003chr\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" State-affiliated sources (RT, Xinhua, IRNA) are included for completeness but visually tagged so analysts can factor in editorial bias. Legacy endpoints in \u003ccode\u003eapi/*.js\u003c/code\u003e each handle a single data source concern — proxying, caching, or transforming external APIs. The newer proto-first endpoints route through a single edge gateway (\u003ccode\u003eapi/[domain]/v1/[rpc].ts\u003c/code\u003e) that dispatches to typed handler implementations generated from Protocol Buffer definitions (see \u003ca href=\"#proto-first-api-contracts\"\u003eProto-First API Contracts\u003c/a\u003e). Both generations coexist, with new features built proto-first. This architecture avoids a monolithic backend while keeping API keys server-side:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRSS Proxy\u003c/strong\u003e — domain-allowlisted proxy for 100+ feeds, preventing CORS issues and hiding origin servers. Feeds from domains that block Vercel IPs are automatically routed through the Railway relay.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAI Pipeline\u003c/strong\u003e — Groq and OpenRouter edge functions with Redis deduplication, so identical headlines across concurrent users only trigger one LLM call. The classify-event endpoint pauses its queue on 500 errors to avoid wasting API quota.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eData Adapters\u003c/strong\u003e — GDELT, ACLED, OpenSky, USGS, NASA FIRMS, FRED, Yahoo Finance, CoinGecko, mempool.space, BIS, WTO, and others each have dedicated edge functions that normalize responses into consistent schemas\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMarket Intelligence\u003c/strong\u003e — macro signals, ETF flows, and stablecoin monitors compute derived analytics server-side (VWAP, SMA, peg deviation, flow estimates) and cache results in Redis\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTemporal Baseline\u003c/strong\u003e — Welford's algorithm state is persisted in Redis across requests, building statistical baselines without a traditional database\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCustom Scrapers\u003c/strong\u003e — sources without RSS feeds (FwdStart, GitHub Trending, tech events) are scraped and transformed into RSS-compatible formats\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFinance Geo Data\u003c/strong\u003e — stock exchanges (92), financial centers (19), central banks (13), and commodity hubs (10) are served as static typed datasets with market caps, GFCI rankings, trading hours, and commodity specializations\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBIS Integration\u003c/strong\u003e — policy rates, real effective exchange rates, and credit-to-GDP ratios from the Bank for International Settlements, cached with 30-minute TTL\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWTO Trade Policy\u003c/strong\u003e — trade restrictions, tariff trends, bilateral trade flows, and SPS/TBT barriers from the World Trade Organization\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSupply Chain Intelligence\u003c/strong\u003e — maritime chokepoint disruption scores (cross-referencing NGA warnings + AIS data), FRED shipping freight indices with spike detection, and critical mineral supply concentration via Herfindahl-Hirschman Index analysis\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAll edge functions include circuit breaker logic and return cached stale data when upstream APIs are unavailable, ensuring the dashboard never shows blank panels.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" The Railway relay server acts as an alternate origin, handling:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAIS vessel tracking\u003c/strong\u003e — maintains a persistent WebSocket connection to AISStream.io and multiplexes it to all connected browser clients, avoiding per-user connection limits\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOpenSky aircraft data\u003c/strong\u003e — authenticates via OAuth2 client credentials flow (Vercel IPs get 403'd by OpenSky without auth tokens)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRSS feeds\u003c/strong\u003e — proxies feeds from domains that block Vercel IPs, with a separate domain allowlist for security\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe Vercel edge functions connect to Railway via \u003ccode\u003eWS_RELAY_URL\u003c/code\u003e (server-side, HTTPS) while browser clients connect via \u003ccode\u003eVITE_WS_RELAY_URL\u003c/code\u003e (client-side, WSS). This separation keeps the relay URL configurable per deployment without leaking server-side configuration to the browser.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAll Railway relay responses are gzip-compressed (zlib \u003ccode\u003egzipSync\u003c/code\u003e) when the client accepts it and the payload exceeds 1KB, reducing egress by ~80% for JSON and XML responses. The desktop local sidecar now prefers Brotli (\u003ccode\u003ebr\u003c/code\u003e) and falls back to gzip for payloads larger than 1KB, setting \u003ccode\u003eContent-Encoding\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eVary: Accept-Encoding\u003c/code\u003e automatically.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eAPI keys are stored in the operating system's credential manager (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager) — never in plaintext config files. All secrets are consolidated into a single JSON vault entry in the keychain, so app startup requires exactly one OS authorization prompt regardless of how many keys are configured.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAt sidecar launch, the vault is read, parsed, and injected as environment variables. Empty or whitespace-only values are skipped. Secrets can also be updated at runtime without restarting the sidecar: saving a key in the Settings window triggers a \u003ccode\u003ePOST /api/local-env-update\u003c/code\u003e call that hot-patches \u003ccode\u003eprocess.env\u003c/code\u003e so handlers pick up the new value immediately.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eVerification pipeline\u003c/strong\u003e — when you enter a credential in Settings, the app validates it against the actual provider API (Groq → \u003ccode\u003e/openai/v1/models\u003c/code\u003e, Ollama → \u003ccode\u003e/api/tags\u003c/code\u003e, FRED → GDP test query, NASA FIRMS → fire data fetch, etc.). Network errors (timeouts, DNS failures, unreachable hosts) are treated as soft passes — the key is saved with a \"could not verify\" notice rather than blocking. Only explicit 401/403 responses from the provider mark a key as invalid. This prevents transient network issues from locking users out of their own credentials.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSmart re-verification\u003c/strong\u003e — when saving settings, the verification pipeline skips keys that haven't been modified since their last successful verification. This prevents unnecessary round-trips to provider APIs when a user changes one key but has 15 others already configured and validated. Only newly entered or modified keys trigger verification requests.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDesktop-specific requirements\u003c/strong\u003e — some features require fewer credentials on desktop than on the web. For example, AIS vessel tracking on the web requires both a relay URL and an API key, but the desktop sidecar handles relay connections internally, so only the API key is needed. The settings panel adapts its required-fields display based on the detected platform.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eSidecar Authentication\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-sidecar-authentication\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Sidecar Authentication\" href=\"#sidecar-authentication\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA unique 32-character hex token is generated per app launch using randomized hash state (\u003ccode\u003eRandomState\u003c/code\u003e from Rust's standard library). dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe sidecar defaults to port 46123 but handles \u003ccode\u003eEADDRINUSE\u003c/code\u003e gracefully — if the port is occupied (another World Monitor instance, or any other process), the sidecar binds to port 0 and lets the OS assign an available ephemeral port. The actual bound port is written to a port file (\u003ccode\u003esidecar.port\u003c/code\u003e in the logs directory) that the Rust host polls on startup (100ms intervals, 5-second timeout). The frontend discovers the port at runtime via the \u003ccode\u003eget_local_api_port\u003c/code\u003e IPC command, and \u003ccode\u003egetApiBaseUrl()\u003c/code\u003e in \u003ccode\u003eruntime.ts\u003c/code\u003e is the canonical accessor — hardcoding port 46123 in frontend code is prohibited. The CSP \u003ccode\u003econnect-src\u003c/code\u003e directive uses \u003ccode\u003ehttp://127.0.0.1:*\u003c/code\u003e to accommodate any port.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eLocal RSS Proxy\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-local-rss-proxy\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Local RSS Proxy\" href=\"#local-rss-proxy\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe sidecar includes a built-in RSS proxy handler that fetches news feeds directly from source domains, bypassing the cloud RSS proxy entirely. This means the desktop app can load all 150+ RSS feeds without any cloud dependency — the same domain allowlist used by the Vercel edge proxy is enforced locally. Combined with the local API handlers, this enables the desktop app to operate as a fully self-contained intelligence aggregation platform.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eSidecar Resilience\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-sidecar-resilience\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Sidecar Resilience\" href=\"#sidecar-resilience\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe sidecar employs multiple resilience patterns to maintain data availability when upstream APIs degrade:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStale-on-error\u003c/strong\u003e — when an upstream API returns a 5xx error or times out, the sidecar serves the last successful response from its in-memory cache rather than propagating the failure. Panels display stale data with a visual \"retrying\" indicator rather than going blank\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNegative caching\u003c/strong\u003e — after an upstream failure, the sidecar records a 5-minute negative cache entry to prevent immediately re-hitting the same broken endpoint. Subsequent requests during the cooldown receive the stale response instantly\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStaggered requests\u003c/strong\u003e — APIs with strict rate limits (Yahoo Finance) use sequential request batching with 150ms inter-request delays instead of \u003ccode\u003ePromise.all\u003c/code\u003e. This transforms 10 concurrent requests that would trigger HTTP 429 into a staggered sequence that stays under rate limits\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eIn-flight deduplication\u003c/strong\u003e — concurrent requests for the same resource (e.g., multiple panels polling the same endpoint) are collapsed into a single upstream fetch. The first request creates a Promise stored in an in-flight map; all concurrent requests await that single Promise\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePanel retry indicator\u003c/strong\u003e — when a panel's data fetch fails and retries, the Panel base class displays a non-intrusive \"Retrying...\" indicator so users understand the dashboard is self-healing rather than broken\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eCloud Fallback\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-cloud-fallback\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Cloud Fallback\" href=\"#cloud-fallback\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhen a local API handler is missing, throws an error, or returns a 5xx status, the sidecar transparently proxies the request to the cloud deployment. The first request for a given resource key (e.g., an RSS feed URL or OpenSky bounding box) creates a Promise stored in an in-flight Map. All concurrent requests for the same key await that single Promise rather than stampeding the upstream API. Subsequent requests are served from cache with an \u003ccode\u003eX-Cache: DEDUP\u003c/code\u003e header. This prevents scenarios like 53 concurrent RSS cache misses or 5 simultaneous OpenSky requests for the same geographic region — all resolved by a single upstream fetch.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv ────────────────┘\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eTier\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eScope\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eTTL\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003ePurpose\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eIn-memory\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003ePer paths\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRedis (Upstash)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eCross-user, cross-instance\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eVaries (120s–900s)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eDeduplicates API calls across all (\u003ccode\u003eopensky:v2:lamin=...\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003emacro-signals:v2:default\u003c/code\u003e) so schema changes don't serve stale formats. Every response includes an \u003ccode\u003eX-Cache\u003c/code\u003e header (\u003ccode\u003eHIT\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eREDIS-HIT\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eMISS\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eREDIS-STALE\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eREDIS-ERROR-FALLBACK\u003c/code\u003e) for debugging.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eShared caching layer\u003c/strong\u003e — all sebuf handler implementations share a unified Upstash Redis caching module (\u003ccode\u003e_upstash-cache.js\u003c/code\u003e) with a consistent API: \u003ccode\u003egetCachedOrFetch(cacheKey, ttlSeconds, fetchFn)\u003c/code\u003e. This eliminates per-handler caching boilerplate and ensures every RPC endpoint benefits from the three-tier strategy. Cache keys include request-varying parameters (e.g., requested symbols, country codes, bounding boxes) to prevent cache contamination across callers with different inputs. On desktop, the same module runs in the sidecar with an in-memory + persistent file backend when Redis is unavailable.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eIn-flight promise deduplication\u003c/strong\u003e — the \u003ccode\u003ecachedFetchJson\u003c/code\u003e function in \u003ccode\u003eserver/_shared/redis.ts\u003c/code\u003e maintains an in-memory \u003ccode\u003eMap\u0026lt;string, Promise\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e of active upstream requests. When a cache miss occurs, the first caller's fetch creates and registers a Promise in the map. All concurrent callers for the same cache key await that single Promise rather than independently hitting the upstream API. This eliminates the \"thundering herd\" problem where multiple edge function instances simultaneously race to refill an expired cache entry — a scenario that previously caused 50+ concurrent upstream requests during the ~15-second refill window for popular endpoints.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe AI summarization pipeline adds content-based deduplication: headlines are hashed and checked against Redis before calling Groq, so the same breaking news viewed by 1,000 concurrent users triggers exactly one LLM call.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" Requests for unlisted domains are rejected with 403.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRailway domain allowlist\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThe Railway relay has a separate, smaller domain allowlist for feeds that need the alternate origin.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAPI key isolation\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAll API keys live server-side in Vercel environment variables. The browser never sees Groq, OpenRouter, ACLED, Finnhub, or other credentials.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eInput sanitization\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eUser-facing content passes through \u003ccode\u003eescapeHtml()\u003c/code\u003e (prevents XSS) and \u003ccode\u003esanitizeUrl()\u003c/code\u003e (blocks \u003ccode\u003ejavascript:\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003edata:\u003c/code\u003e URIs). URLs use \u003ccode\u003eescapeAttr()\u003c/code\u003e for attribute context encoding.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eQuery parameter validation\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAPI endpoints validate input formats (e.g., stablecoin coin IDs must match \u003ccode\u003e[a-z0-9-]+\u003c/code\u003e, bounding box params are numeric).\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eIP rate limiting\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAI endpoints use Upstash Redis-backed rate limiting to prevent abuse of Groq/OpenRouter quotas.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDesktop sidecar auth\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThe local API sidecar requires a per-session \u003ccode\u003eBearer\u003c/code\u003e token generated at launch. The token is stored in Rust state and injected into the sidecar environment — only the Tauri frontend can retrieve it via IPC. Health check endpoints are exempt.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOS keychain storage\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eDesktop API keys are stored in the operating system's credential manager (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager), never in plaintext files or environment variables on disk.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBot-aware social previews\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003e/api/story\u003c/code\u003e endpoint detects social crawlers (10+ signatures: Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, Telegram, Discord, Reddit, WhatsApp, Google) and serves OG-tagged HTML with dynamic preview images. Regular browsers receive a 302 redirect to the SPA.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBot protection middleware\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eEdge Middleware blocks crawlers and scrapers from all \u003ccode\u003e/api/*\u003c/code\u003e routes — bot user-agents and requests with short or missing \u003ccode\u003eUser-Agent\u003c/code\u003e headers receive 403. Social preview bots are selectively allowed on \u003ccode\u003e/api/story\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003e/api/og-story\u003c/code\u003e for Open Graph image generation. Reinforced by \u003ccode\u003erobots.txt\u003c/code\u003e Disallow rules on API paths.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNo debug endpoints\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003eapi/debug-env.js\u003c/code\u003e endpoint returns 404 in production — it exists only as a disabled placeholder.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSSRF protection\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThe desktop sidecar's RSS proxy runs two-phase URL validation: protocol allowlist (HTTP/HTTPS only), private IP rejection (all RFC-1918 ranges, link-local, multicast, IPv6-mapped v4), DNS resolution to detect rebinding attacks, and \u003cstrong\u003eTOCTOU-safe pinning\u003c/strong\u003e — the first resolved IPv4 address is locked for the actual TCP connection, preventing DNS rebinding between check and connect.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eIPC window hardening\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAll sensitive Tauri IPC commands (keychain access, token retrieval, cache operations, Polymarket bridge) gate on \u003ccode\u003erequire_trusted_window()\u003c/code\u003e. Only windows with labels in the \u003ccode\u003eTRUSTED_WINDOWS\u003c/code\u003e allowlist (\u003ccode\u003emain\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003esettings\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003elive-channels\u003c/code\u003e) can invoke these commands — injected iframes or rogue webviews receive an explicit rejection.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDevTools gating\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThe developer tools menu item and its \u003ccode\u003eCmd+Alt+I\u003c/code\u003e keybinding only compile into the binary when the \u003ccode\u003edevtools\u003c/code\u003e Cargo feature is enabled. Production builds omit the feature entirely, so DevTools cannot be opened in shipped binaries regardless of UI manipulation.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003chr\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" environment-aware routing (production on \u003ccode\u003eworldmonitor.app\u003c/code\u003e, preview on \u003ccode\u003e*.vercel.app\u003c/code\u003e, disabled on localhost and Tauri desktop).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe configuration includes 30+ \u003ccode\u003eignoreErrors\u003c/code\u003e patterns that suppress noise from:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThird-party WebView injections\u003c/strong\u003e — Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram in-app browsers inject scripts that reference undefined variables (\u003ccode\u003eCONFIG\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecurrentInset\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBrowser extensions\u003c/strong\u003e — Chrome/Firefox extensions that fail \u003ccode\u003eimportScripts\u003c/code\u003e or violate CSP policies\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWebGL context loss\u003c/strong\u003e — transient GPU crashes in MapLibre/deck.gl that self-recover\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eiOS Safari quirks\u003c/strong\u003e — IndexedDB connection drops on background tab kills, \u003ccode\u003eNotAllowedError\u003c/code\u003e from autoplay policies\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNetwork transients\u003c/strong\u003e — \u003ccode\u003eTypeError: Failed to fetch\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eTypeError: Load failed\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eTypeError: cancelled\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMapLibre internal crashes\u003c/strong\u003e — null-access in style layers, light, and placement that originate from the map chunk\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA custom \u003ccode\u003ebeforeSend\u003c/code\u003e hook provides second-stage filtering: it suppresses single-character error messages (minification artifacts), \u003ccode\u003eImporting a module script failed\u003c/code\u003e errors from browser extensions (identified by \u003ccode\u003echrome-extension:\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003emoz-extension:\u003c/code\u003e in the stack trace), and MapLibre internal null-access crashes when the stack trace originates from map chunk files.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eChunk reload guard\u003c/strong\u003e — after deployments, users with stale browser tabs may encounter \u003ccode\u003evite:preloadError\u003c/code\u003e events when dynamically imported chunks have new content-hash filenames. The guard listens for this event and performs a one-shot page reload, using \u003ccode\u003esessionStorage\u003c/code\u003e to prevent infinite reload loops. If the reload succeeds (app initializes fully), the guard flag is cleared. This recovers gracefully from stale-asset 404s without requiring users to manually refresh.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStorage quota management\u003c/strong\u003e — when a device's localStorage or IndexedDB quota is exhausted (common on mobile Safari with its 5MB limit), a global \u003ccode\u003e_storageQuotaExceeded\u003c/code\u003e flag disables all further write attempts across both the persistent cache (IndexedDB + localStorage fallback) and the utility \u003ccode\u003esaveToStorage()\u003c/code\u003e function. The flag is set on the first \u003ccode\u003eDOMException\u003c/code\u003e with \u003ccode\u003ename === 'QuotaExceededError'\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003ecode === 22\u003c/code\u003e, and prevents cascading errors from repeated failed writes. Read operations continue normally — cached data remains accessible, only new writes are suppressed.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTransactions are sampled at 10% to balance observability with cost. Release tracking (\u003ccode\u003eworldmonitor@{version}\u003c/code\u003e) enables regression detection across deployments.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eQuick Start\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-quick-start\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Quick Start\" href=\"#quick-start\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"# Clone and run\ngit clone https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor.git\ncd worldmonitor\nnpm install\nvercel dev       # <ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>150+ RSS feeds</strong> across geopolitics, defense, energy, tech, and finance — domain-allowlisted proxy prevents CORS issues. Each variant loads its own curated feed set: ~25 categories for geopolitical, ~20 for tech, ~18 for finance</li>

<li><strong>Idle-aware playback</strong> — video players pause and are removed from the DOM after 5 minutes of inactivity, resuming when the user returns. Tab visibility changes also suspend/resume streams</li>
<li><strong>Global streaming quality control</strong> — a user-selectable quality setting (auto, 360p, 480p, 720p) that applies to all live video streams across the dashboard. The preference persists in localStorage and propagates to active players via a <code>stream-quality-changed</code> CustomEvent — no reload required when switching quality</li>
<li><strong>19 live webcams</strong> — real-time YouTube streams from geopolitical hotspots across 4 regions (Middle East, Europe, Americas, Asia-Pacific). Grid view shows 4 strategic feeds simultaneously; single-feed view available. Region filtering (ALL/MIDEAST/EUROPE/AMERICAS/ASIA), idle-aware playback that pauses after 5 minutes, and Intersection Observer-based lazy loading</li>
<li><strong>Custom keyword monitors</strong> — user-defined keyword alerts with word-boundary matching (prevents "ai" from matching "train"), automatic color-coding from a 10-color palette, and multi-keyword support (comma-separated). <li><strong>Entity extraction</strong> — Auto-links countries, leaders, organizations</li>
<li><strong>Instant flat render</strong> — news items appear immediately as a flat list the moment feed data arrives. Finance variant categories fetch with 5 concurrent requests (vs 3) for ~10–15 second faster cold starts</li>
<li><strong>Virtual scrolling</strong> — news panels with 15+ items use a custom virtual list renderer that only creates DOM elements for visible items plus a 3-item overscan buffer. </ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Country Brief Pages</h3><a id="user-content-country-brief-pages" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Country Brief Pages" href="#country-brief-pages"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Clicking any country on the map opens a full-page intelligence dossier — a single-screen synthesis of all intelligence modules for that country. The brief is organized into a two-column layout:</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Left column</strong>:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Instability Index</strong> — animated SVG score ring (0–100) with four component breakdown bars (Unrest, Conflict, Security, Information), severity badge, and trend indicator</li>
<li><strong>Intelligence Brief</strong> — AI-generated analysis (Ollama local / Groq / OpenRouter, depending on configured provider) with inline citation anchors <code>[1]</code>–<code>[8]</code> that scroll to the corresponding news source when clicked</li>
<li><strong>Top News</strong> — 8 most relevant headlines for the country, threat-level color-coded, with source and time-ago metadata</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Right column</strong>:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Active Signals</strong> — real-time chip indicators for protests, military aircraft, naval vessels, internet outages, earthquakes, displacement flows, climate stress, conflict events, and the country's stock market index (1-week change)</li>
<li><strong>7-Day Timeline</strong> — D3.js-rendered event chart with 4 severity-coded lanes (protest, conflict, natural, military), interactive tooltips, and responsive resizing</li>
<li><strong>Prediction Markets</strong> — top 3 Polymarket contracts by volume with probability bars and external links</li>
<li><strong>Infrastructure Exposure</strong> — pipelines, undersea cables, datacenters, military bases, nuclear facilities, and ports within a 600km radius of the country centroid, ranked by distance</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Headline relevance filtering</strong>: each country has an alias map (e.g., <code>US → ["united states", "american", "washington", "pentagon", "biden", "trump"]</code>). Headlines are filtered using a negative-match algorithm — if another country's alias appears earlier in the headline title than the target country's alias, the headline is excluded. This prevents cross-contamination (e.g., a headline about Venezuela mentioning "Washington sanctions" appearing in the US brief).</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Export options</strong>: briefs are exportable as JSON (structured data with all scores, signals, and headlines), CSV (flattened tabular format), or PNG image. A print button triggers the browser's native print dialog for PDF export.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Local-First Country Detection</h3><a id="user-content-local-first-country-detection" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Local-First Country Detection" href="#local-first-country-detection"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Map clicks resolve to countries using a local geometry service rather than relying on network reverse-geocoding (Nominatim). The system loads a GeoJSON file containing polygon boundaries for ~200 countries and builds an indexed spatial lookup:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li><strong>Bounding box pre-filter</strong> — each country's polygon(s) are wrapped in a bounding box (<code>[minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat]</code>). Points outside the bbox are rejected without polygon intersection testing.</li>
<li><strong>Ray-casting algorithm</strong> — for points inside the bbox, a ray is cast from the point along the positive x-axis. The number of polygon edge intersections determines inside/outside status (odd = inside). Edge cases are handled: points on segment boundaries return <code>true</code>, and polygon holes are subtracted (a point inside an outer ring but also inside a hole is excluded).</li>
<li><strong>MultiPolygon support</strong> — countries with non-contiguous territories (e.g., the US with Alaska and Hawaii, Indonesia with thousands of islands) use MultiPolygon geometries where each polygon is tested independently.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">This approach provides sub-millisecond country detection entirely in the browser, with no network latency. The geometry data is preloaded at app startup and cached for the session. For countries not in the GeoJSON (rare), the system falls back to hardcoded rectangular bounding boxes, and finally to network reverse-geocoding as a last resort.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">AI Summarization Chain</h3><a id="user-content-ai-summarization-chain" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: AI Summarization Chain" href="#ai-summarization-chain"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

│  Local endpoint, no cloud       │               │
│  Auto-discovered model          │               │

<p dir="auto">All three API tiers (Ollama, Groq, OpenRouter) share a common handler factory (<code>_summarize-handler.js</code>) that provides identical behavior:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Headline deduplication</strong> — before sending to any LLM, headlines are compared pairwise using word-overlap similarity. Near-duplicates (>60% overlap) are merged, reducing the prompt by 20–40% and preventing the LLM from wasting tokens on repeated stories</li>
<li><strong>Variant-aware prompting</strong> — the system prompt adapts to the active dashboard variant. Geopolitical summaries emphasize conflict escalation and diplomatic shifts; tech summaries focus on funding rounds and AI breakthroughs; finance summaries highlight market movements and central bank signals</li>
<li><strong>Language-aware output</strong> — when the UI language is non-English, the prompt instructs the LLM to generate the summary in that language</li>
<li><strong>Redis deduplication</strong> — summaries are cached with a composite key (<code>summary:v3:{mode}:{variant}:{lang}:{hash}</code>) so the same headlines viewed by 1,000 concurrent users trigger exactly one LLM call. Cache TTL is 24 hours</li>
<li><strong>Graceful fallback</strong> — if a provider returns <code>{fallback: true}</code> (missing API key or endpoint unreachable), the chain silently advances to the next tier. Progress callbacks update the UI to show which provider is being attempted</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">The Ollama tier communicates via the OpenAI-compatible <code>/v1/chat/completions</code> endpoint, making it compatible with any local inference server that implements this standard (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp server, vLLM, etc.).</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Threat Classification Pipeline</h3><a id="user-content-threat-classification-pipeline" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Threat Classification Pipeline" href="#threat-classification-pipeline"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Every news item passes through a three-stage classification pipeline:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Keyword classifier</strong> (instant, <code>source: 'keyword'</code>) — pattern-matches against ~120 threat keywords organized by severity tier (critical → high → medium → low → info) and 14 event categories (conflict, protest, disaster, diplomatic, economic, terrorism, cyber, health, environmental, military, crime, infrastructure, tech, general). Keywords use word-boundary regex matching to prevent false positives (e.g., "war" won't match "award"). Each match returns a severity level, category, and confidence score. Variant-specific keyword sets ensure the tech variant doesn't flag "sanctions" in non-geopolitical contexts.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Browser-side ML</strong> (async, <code>source: 'ml'</code>) — Transformers.js runs NER, sentiment analysis, and topic classification directly in the browser with no server dependency. Provides a second classification opinion without any API call.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>LLM classifier</strong> (batched async, <code>source: 'llm'</code>) — headlines are collected into a batch queue and fired as parallel <code>classifyEvent</code> RPCs via the sebuf proto client. Each RPC calls the configured LLM provider (Groq Llama 3.1 8B at temperature 0, or Ollama for local inference). Results are cached in Redis (24h TTL) keyed by headline hash. When 500-series errors occur, the LLM classifier automatically pauses its queue to avoid wasting API quota, resuming after an exponential backoff delay. When the LLM result arrives, it overrides the keyword result only if its confidence is higher.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">This hybrid approach means the UI is never blocked waiting for AI — users see keyword results instantly, with ML and LLM refinements arriving within seconds and persisting for all subsequent visitors. Each classification carries its <code>source</code> tag (<code>keyword</code>, <code>ml</code>, or <code>llm</code>) so downstream consumers can weight confidence accordingly.</p>

The score is computed from:</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Hotspot Escalation Scoring</h3><a id="user-content-hotspot-escalation-scoring" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Hotspot Escalation Scoring" href="#hotspot-escalation-scoring"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Intelligence hotspots receive dynamic escalation scores blending four normalized signals (0–100):</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>News activity</strong> (35%) — article count and severity in the hotspot's area</li>
<li><strong>Country instability</strong> (25%) — CII score of the host country</li>
<li><strong>Geo-convergence alerts</strong> (25%) — spatial binning detects 3+ event types (protests + military + earthquakes) co-occurring within 1° lat/lon cells</li>
<li><strong>Military activity</strong> (15%) — vessel clusters and flight density near the hotspot</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">The system blends static baseline risk (40%) with detected events (60%) and tracks trends via linear regression on 48-hour history. Signal emissions cool down for 2 hours to prevent alert fatigue.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Geographic Convergence Detection</h3><a id="user-content-geographic-convergence-detection" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Geographic Convergence Detection" href="#geographic-convergence-detection"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Events (protests, military flights, vessels, earthquakes) are binned into 1°×1° geographic cells within a 24-hour window. When 3+ distinct event types converge in one cell, a convergence alert fires. Scoring is based on type diversity (×25pts per unique type) plus event count bonuses (×2pts). Alerts are reverse-geocoded to human-readable names using conflict zones, waterways, and hotspot databases.</p>
