<p dir="auto">The dashboard ingests weekly U.S. Naval Institute (USNI) fleet deployment reports and merges them with live AIS vessel tracking data. Each report is parsed for carrier strike groups, amphibious ready groups, and individual combatant deployments — extracting hull numbers, vessel names, operational regions, and mission notes.</p>
<p dir="auto">The merge algorithm matches USNI entries against live AIS-tracked vessels by hull number and normalized name. Matched vessels receive enrichment: strike group assignment, deployment status (deployed / returning / in-port), and operational theater. Unmatched USNI entries (submarines, vessels running dark) generate synthetic positions based on the last known operational region, with coordinate scattering to prevent marker overlap.</p>
<p dir="auto">This dual-source approach provides a more complete operational picture than either AIS or USNI alone — AIS reveals real-time positions but misses submarines and vessels with transponders off, while USNI captures the complete order of battle but with weekly lag.</p>

<p dir="auto">Enrichment queries are batched (up to 50 aircraft per request) and cached with a circuit breaker pattern to avoid hammering the upstream API during high-traffic periods. The enriched metadata feeds into the Theater Posture Assessment — a KC-135 tanker paired with F-15s and an E-3 AWACS indicates strike packaging, not routine training.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Undersea Cable Health Monitoring</h3><a id="user-content-undersea-cable-health-monitoring" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Undersea Cable Health Monitoring" href="#undersea-cable-health-monitoring"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Beyond displaying static cable routes on the map, the system actively monitors cable health by cross-referencing two live data sources:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>NGA Navigational Warnings</strong> — the U.S. National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency publishes maritime safety broadcasts that frequently mention cable repair operations. The system filters these warnings for cable-related keywords (<code>CABLE</code>, <code>CABLESHIP</code>, <code>SUBMARINE CABLE</code>, <code>FIBER OPTIC</code>, etc.) and extracts structured data: vessel names, DMS/decimal coordinates, advisory severity, and repair ETAs. Each warning is matched to the nearest cataloged undersea cable within a 5° geographic radius.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>AIS Cable Ship Tracking</strong> — dedicated cable repair vessels (CS Reliance, Île de Bréhat, Cable Innovator, etc.) are identified by name pattern matching against AIS transponder data. Ship status is classified as <code>enroute</code> (transiting to repair site) or <code>on-station</code> (actively working) based on keyword analysis of the warning text.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Advisories are classified by severity: <code>fault</code> (cable break, cut, or damage — potential traffic rerouting) or <code>degraded</code> (repair work in progress with partial capacity). Impact descriptions are generated dynamically, linking the advisory to the specific cable and the countries it serves — enabling questions like "which cables serving South Asia are currently under repair?"</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Health scoring algorithm</strong> — Each cable receives a composite health score (0–100) computed from weighted signals with exponential time decay:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto"><pre class="notranslate"><code>signal_weight = severity × (e^(-λ × age_hours))     where λ = ln(2) / 168 (7-day half-life)

</code></pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

<p dir="auto">Signals are classified into two kinds: <code>operator_fault</code> (confirmed cable damage — severity 1.0) and <code>cable_advisory</code> (repair operations, navigational warnings — severity 0.6). Geographic matching uses cosine-latitude-corrected equirectangular approximation to find the nearest cataloged cable within 50km of each NGA warning's coordinates. Results are cached in Redis (6-hour TTL for complete results, 10 minutes for partial) with an in-memory fallback that serves stale data when Redis is unavailable — ensuring the cable health layer never shows blank data even during cache failures.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Infrastructure Cascade Modeling</h3><a id="user-content-infrastructure-cascade-modeling" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Infrastructure Cascade Modeling" href="#infrastructure-cascade-modeling"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<p dir="auto"><strong>Impact calculation</strong>: <code>strength = edge_weight × disruption_level × (1 − redundancy)</code></p>
<p dir="auto">Strategic chokepoint modeling captures real-world dependencies:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Strait of Hormuz</strong> — 80% of Japan's oil, 70% of South Korea's, 60% of India's, 40% of China's</li>
<li><strong>Suez Canal</strong> — EU-Asia trade routes (Germany, Italy, UK, China)</li>
<li><strong>Malacca Strait</strong> — 80% of China's oil transit</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Ports are weighted by type: oil/LNG terminals (0.9 — critical), container ports (0.7), naval bases (0.4 — geopolitical but less economic). This enables questions like "if the Strait of Hormuz closes, which countries face energy shortages within 30 days?"</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Related Assets & Proximity Correlation</h3><a id="user-content-related-assets--proximity-correlation" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Related Assets & Proximity Correlation" href="#related-assets--proximity-correlation"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">When a news event is geo-located, the system automatically identifies critical infrastructure within a 600km radius — pipelines, undersea cables, data centers, military bases, and nuclear facilities — ranked by distance. This enables instant geopolitical context: a cable cut near a strategic chokepoint, a protest near a nuclear facility, or troop movements near a data center cluster.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">News Geo-Location</h3><a id="user-content-news-geo-location" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: News Geo-Location" href="#news-geo-location"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">A 74-hub strategic location database infers geography from headlines via keyword matching. Hubs span capitals, conflict zones, strategic chokepoints (Strait of Hormuz, Suez Canal, Malacca Strait), and international organizations. Confidence scoring is boosted for critical-tier hubs and active conflict zones, enabling map-driven news placement without requiring explicit location metadata from RSS feeds.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Entity Index & Cross-Referencing</h3><a id="user-content-entity-index--cross-referencing" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Entity Index & Cross-Referencing" href="#entity-index--cross-referencing"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">A structured entity registry catalogs countries, organizations, world leaders, and military entities with multiple lookup indices:</p>

<p dir="auto">Entity matching uses word-boundary regex to prevent false positives (e.g., "Iran" matching "Ukraine"). Confidence scores are tiered by match quality: exact name matches score 1.0, aliases 0.85–0.95, and keyword matches 0.7. When the same entity surfaces across multiple independent data sources (news, military tracking, protest feeds, market signals), the system identifies it as a focal point and escalates its prominence in the intelligence picture.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Temporal Baseline Anomaly Detection</h3><a id="user-content-temporal-baseline-anomaly-detection" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Temporal Baseline Anomaly Detection" href="#temporal-baseline-anomaly-detection"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Rather than relying on static thresholds, the system learns what "normal" looks like and flags deviations. Each event type (military flights, naval vessels, protests, news velocity, AIS gaps, satellite fires) is tracked per region with separate baselines for each weekday and month — because military activity patterns differ on Tuesdays vs. weekends, and January vs. July.</p>
<p dir="auto">The algorithm uses <strong>Welford's online method</strong> for numerically stable streaming computation of mean and variance, stored in Redis with a 90-day rolling window. When a new observation arrives, its z-score is computed against the learned baseline. Thresholds:</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table data-catalyst=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Z-Score</th>
<th>Severity</th>
<th>Example</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>≥ 1.5</td>
<td>Low</td>
<td>Slightly elevated protest activity</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>≥ 2.0</td>
<td>Medium</td>
<td>Unusual naval presence</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>≥ 3.0</td>
<td>High/Critical</td>
<td>Military flights 3x above baseline</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto">A minimum of 10 historical samples is required before anomalies are reported, preventing false positives during the learning phase. Anomalies are ingested back into the signal aggregator, where they compound with other signals for convergence detection.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Trending Keyword Spike Detection</h3><a id="user-content-trending-keyword-spike-detection" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Trending Keyword Spike Detection" href="#trending-keyword-spike-detection"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Every RSS headline is tokenized into individual terms and tracked in per-term frequency maps. A 2-hour rolling window captures current activity while a 7-day baseline (refreshed hourly) establishes what "normal" looks like for each term. A spike fires when all conditions are met:</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table data-catalyst=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Condition</th>
<th>Threshold</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Absolute count</strong></td>
<td>> <code>minSpikeCount</code> (5 mentions)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Relative surge</strong></td>
<td>> baseline × <code>spikeMultiplier</code> (3×)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Source diversity</strong></td>
<td>≥ 2 unique RSS feed sources</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Cooldown</strong></td>
<td>30 minutes since last spike for the same term</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto">The tokenizer extracts CVE identifiers (<code>CVE-2024-xxxxx</code>), APT/FIN threat actor designators, and 12 compound terms for world leaders (e.g., "Xi Jinping", "Kim Jong Un") that would be lost by naive whitespace splitting. A configurable blocklist suppresses common noise terms.</p>
<p dir="auto">Detected spikes are auto-summarized via Groq (rate-limited to 5 summaries/hour) and emitted as <code>keyword_spike</code> signals into the correlation engine, where they compound with other signal types for convergence detection. The term registry is capped at 10,000 entries with LRU eviction to bound memory usage. All thresholds (spike multiplier, min count, cooldown, blocked terms) are configurable via the Settings panel.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Proto-First API Contracts</h3><a id="user-content-proto-first-api-contracts" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Proto-First API Contracts" href="#proto-first-api-contracts"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<p dir="auto"><strong>Code generation pipeline</strong> — a <code>Makefile</code> drives <code>buf generate</code> with three custom sebuf protoc plugins:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li><code>protoc-gen-ts-client</code> → typed fetch-based client classes (<code>src/generated/client/</code>)</li>
<li><code>protoc-gen-ts-server</code> → handler interfaces and route descriptors (<code>src/generated/server/</code>)</li>
<li><code>protoc-gen-openapiv3</code> → OpenAPI 3.1.0 specs in YAML and JSON (<code>docs/api/</code>)</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Proto definitions include <code>buf.validate</code> field constraints (e.g., latitude ∈ [−90, 90]), so request validation is generated automatically — handlers receive pre-validated data. Breaking changes are caught at CI time via <code>buf breaking</code> against the main branch.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Edge gateway</strong> — a single Vercel Edge Function (<code>api/[domain]/v1/[rpc].ts</code>) imports all 20 <code>createServiceRoutes()</code> functions into a flat <code>Map<string, handler></code> router. Every RPC is a POST endpoint at a static path (e.g., <code>POST /api/aviation/v1/list-airport-delays</code>), with CORS enforcement, a top-level error boundary that hides internal details on 5xx responses, and rate-limit support (<code>retryAfter</code> on 429). The same router runs locally via a Vite dev-server plugin (<code>sebufApiPlugin</code> in <code>vite.config.ts</code>) with HMR invalidation on handler changes.</p>

<p dir="auto">Each IP-based IOC is geo-enriched using ipinfo.io with freeipapi.com as fallback. Geolocation results are Redis-cached for 24 hours. Enrichment runs concurrently — 16 parallel lookups with a 12-second timeout, processing up to 250 IPs per collection run.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Dual-Source Protest Tracking</h3><a id="user-content-dual-source-protest-tracking" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Dual-Source Protest Tracking" href="#dual-source-protest-tracking"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Protest data is sourced from two independent providers to reduce single-source bias:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li><strong>ACLED</strong> (Armed Conflict Location & Event Data) — 30-day window, tokenized API with Redis caching (10-minute TTL). Covers protests, riots, strikes, and demonstrations with actor attribution and fatality counts.</li>
<li><strong>GDELT</strong> (Global Database of Events, Language, and Tone) — 7-day geospatial event feed filtered to protest keywords. Events with mention count ≥5 are included; those above 30 are marked as <code>validated</code>.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Events from both sources are <strong>Haversine-deduplicated</strong> on a 0.1° grid (~10km) with same-day matching. ACLED events take priority due to higher editorial confidence. Severity is classified as:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>High</strong> — fatalities present or riot/clash keywords</li>
<li><strong>Medium</strong> — standard protest/demonstration</li>
<li><strong>Low</strong> — default</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Protest scoring is regime-aware: democratic countries use logarithmic scaling (routine protests don't trigger instability), while authoritarian states use linear scoring (every protest is significant). Fatalities and concurrent internet outages apply severity boosts.</p>

<p dir="auto"><strong>Hybrid clustering</strong> combines fast Jaccard similarity (n-gram overlap, threshold 0.4) with ML-refined semantic similarity (cosine similarity, threshold 0.78). Jaccard runs instantly on every refresh; semantic refinement runs when the ML worker is loaded and merges clusters that are textually different but semantically identical (e.g., "NATO expands missile shield" and "Alliance deploys new air defense systems").</p>
<p dir="auto">News velocity is tracked per cluster — when multiple Tier 1–2 sources converge on the same story within a short window, the cluster is flagged as a breaking alert with <code>sourcesPerHour</code> as the velocity metric.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Privacy & Offline Architecture</h3><a id="user-content-privacy--offline-architecture" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Privacy & Offline Architecture" href="#privacy--offline-architecture"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">World Monitor is designed so that sensitive intelligence work can run entirely on local hardware with no data leaving the user's machine. The privacy architecture operates at three levels:</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Level 1 — Full Cloud (Web App)</strong>
All processing happens server-side on Vercel Edge Functions. API keys are stored in Vercel environment variables. News feeds are proxied through domain-allowlisted endpoints. AI summaries use Groq or OpenRouter. This is the default for <code>worldmonitor.app</code> — convenient but cloud-dependent.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Level 2 — Desktop with Cloud APIs (Tauri + Sidecar)</strong>
The desktop app runs a local Node.js sidecar that mirrors all 60+ cloud API handlers. API keys are stored in the OS keychain (macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager), never in plaintext files. Requests are processed locally first; cloud is a transparent fallback for missing handlers. Credential management happens through a native settings window with per-key validation.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Level 3 — Air-Gapped Local (Ollama + Desktop)</strong>
With Ollama or LM Studio configured, AI summarization runs entirely on local hardware. Combined with the desktop sidecar, the core intelligence pipeline (news aggregation, threat classification, instability scoring, AI briefings) operates with zero cloud dependency. The browser-side ML pipeline (Transformers.js) provides NER, sentiment analysis, and fallback summarization without even a local server.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Product Analytics</h3><a id="user-content-product-analytics" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Product Analytics" href="#product-analytics"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">World Monitor includes privacy-first product analytics via PostHog to understand usage patterns and improve the dashboard. The implementation enforces strict data safety at multiple levels:</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Typed event allowlists</strong> — every analytics event has a schema defining exactly which properties are permitted. Unlisted properties are silently dropped before transmission. This prevents accidental inclusion of sensitive data in analytics payloads, even if a developer passes extra fields.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>API key stripping</strong> — a <code>sanitize_properties</code> callback runs on every outgoing event. Any string value matching common API key prefixes (<code>sk-</code>, <code>gsk_</code>, <code>or-</code>, <code>Bearer </code>) is replaced with <code>[REDACTED]</code> before it leaves the browser. This is defense-in-depth: even if a key somehow ends up in an event payload, it never reaches the analytics backend.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>No session recordings, no autocapture</strong> — PostHog's session replay and automatic DOM event capture are explicitly disabled. Only explicitly instrumented events are tracked.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Pseudonymous identity</strong> — each installation generates a random UUID stored in localStorage. There is no user login, no email collection, and no cross-device tracking. The UUID is purely pseudonymous — it enables session attribution without identifying individuals.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Ad-blocker bypass</strong> — on the web, PostHog traffic is routed through a reverse proxy on the app's own domain (<code>/ingest</code>) rather than directly to PostHog's servers. This prevents ad blockers from silently dropping analytics requests, ensuring usage data is representative. Desktop builds use PostHog's direct endpoint since ad blockers aren't a factor in native apps.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Offline event queue</strong> — the desktop app may launch without network connectivity. Events captured while offline are queued in localStorage (capped at 200 entries) and flushed to PostHog when connectivity is restored. A <code>window.online</code> listener triggers automatic flush on reconnection.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Super properties</strong> — every event automatically carries platform context: variant (world/tech/finance), app version, platform (web/desktop), screen dimensions, viewport size, device pixel ratio, browser language, and desktop OS/arch. This enables segmentation without per-event instrumentation.</p>
<p dir="auto">30+ typed events cover core user interactions: app load timing, panel views, LLM summary generation (provider, model, cache status), API key configuration snapshots, map layer toggles, variant switches, country brief opens, theme changes, language changes, search usage, panel resizing, webcam selections, and auto-update interactions.</p>
<p dir="auto">Analytics is entirely opt-out by omitting the <code>VITE_POSTHOG_KEY</code> environment variable. When the key is absent, all analytics functions are no-ops with zero runtime overhead.</p>

Rising bilateral tension scores that coincide with military signal spikes in the same region feed into the focal point detection algorithm.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Data Freshness & Intelligence Gaps</h3><a id="user-content-data-freshness--intelligence-gaps" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Data Freshness & Intelligence Gaps" href="#data-freshness--intelligence-gaps"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">A singleton tracker monitors 24 data sources (GDELT, RSS, AIS, military flights, earthquakes, weather, outages, ACLED, Polymarket, economic indicators, NASA FIRMS, cyber threat feeds, trending keywords, oil/energy, population exposure, BIS central bank data, WTO trade policy, and more) with status categorization: fresh (<15 min), stale (1h), very_stale (6h), no_data, error, disabled. It explicitly reports <strong>intelligence gaps</strong> — what analysts can't see — preventing false confidence when critical data sources are down or degraded.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Prediction Markets as Leading Indicators</h3><a id="user-content-prediction-markets-as-leading-indicators" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Prediction Markets as Leading Indicators" href="#prediction-markets-as-leading-indicators"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Polymarket geopolitical markets are queried using tag-based filters (Ukraine, Iran, China, Taiwan, etc.) with 5-minute caching. Market probability shifts are correlated with news volume: if a prediction market moves significantly before matching news arrives, this is flagged as a potential early-warning signal.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Cloudflare JA3 bypass</strong> — Polymarket's API is protected by Cloudflare TLS fingerprinting (JA3) that blocks all server-side requests. The system uses a 3-tier fallback:</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table data-catalyst=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Tier</th>
<th>Method</th>
<th>When It Works</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>1</strong></td>
<td>Browser-direct fetch</td>
<td>Always (browser TLS passes Cloudflare)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>2</strong></td>
<td>Tauri native TLS (reqwest)</td>
<td>Desktop app (Rust TLS fingerprint differs from Node.js)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>3</strong></td>
<td>Vercel edge proxy</td>
<td>Rarely (edge runtime sometimes passes)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto">Once browser-direct succeeds, the system caches this state and skips fallback tiers on subsequent requests. Country-specific markets are fetched by mapping countries to Polymarket tags with name-variant matching (e.g., "Russia" matches titles containing "Russian", "Moscow", "Kremlin", "Putin").</p>
<p dir="auto">Markets are filtered to exclude sports and entertainment (100+ exclusion keywords), require meaningful price divergence from 50% or volume above $50K, and are ranked by trading volume. Each variant gets different tag sets — geopolitical focus queries politics/world/ukraine/middle-east tags, while tech focus queries ai/crypto/business tags.</p>

<p dir="auto">The <code>trade/v1</code> proto service defines four RPCs, each with its own circuit breaker (30-minute cache TTL) and <code>upstreamUnavailable</code> signaling for graceful degradation when WTO endpoints are temporarily unreachable. The panel is available on FULL and FINANCE variants. Trade policy data feeds into the data freshness tracker as <code>wto_trade</code>, with intelligence gap warnings when the WTO feed goes stale.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Supply Chain Disruption Intelligence</h3><a id="user-content-supply-chain-disruption-intelligence" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Supply Chain Disruption Intelligence" href="#supply-chain-disruption-intelligence"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The Supply Chain panel provides real-time visibility into global logistics risk across three complementary dimensions — strategic chokepoint health, shipping cost trends, and critical mineral concentration — enabling early detection of disruptions that cascade into economic and geopolitical consequences.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Chokepoints tab</strong> — monitors 6 strategic maritime bottlenecks (Suez Canal, Strait of Malacca, Strait of Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb, Panama Canal, Taiwan Strait) by cross-referencing live navigational warnings with AIS vessel disruption data. Each chokepoint receives a disruption score (0–100) computed from warning severity and count, mapped to color-coded status indicators (green/yellow/red). Data is cached with a 5-minute TTL for near-real-time awareness.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Shipping Rates tab</strong> — tracks two Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) series: the Deep Sea Freight Producer Price Index (<code>PCU483111483111</code>) and the Freight Transportation Services Index (<code>TSIFRGHT</code>). Statistical spike detection flags abnormal price movements against recent history. Inline SVG sparklines render 24 months of rate history at a glance. Cached for 1 hour to reflect the weekly release cadence of underlying data.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Critical Minerals tab</strong> — applies the <strong>Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI)</strong> to 2024 global production data for minerals critical to technology and defense manufacturing — lithium, cobalt, rare earths, gallium, germanium, and others. The HHI quantifies supply concentration risk: a market dominated by a single producer scores near 10,000, while a perfectly distributed market scores near 0. Each mineral displays the top 3 producing countries with market share percentages, flagging single-country dependencies that represent strategic vulnerability (e.g., China's dominance in rare earth processing). This tab uses static production data, cached for 24 hours with no external API dependency.</p>
<p dir="auto">The panel is available on the FULL (World Monitor) variant and integrates with the infrastructure cascade model — when a chokepoint disruption coincides with high mineral concentration risk for affected trade routes, the combined signal feeds into convergence detection.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">BTC ETF Flow Estimation</h3><a id="user-content-btc-etf-flow-estimation" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: BTC ETF Flow Estimation" href="#btc-etf-flow-estimation"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Ten spot Bitcoin ETFs are tracked via Yahoo Finance's 5-day chart API (IBIT, FBTC, ARKB, BITB, GBTC, HODL, BRRR, EZBC, BTCO, BTCW). Since ETF flow data requires expensive terminal subscriptions, the system estimates flow direction from publicly available signals:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Price change</strong> — daily close vs. previous close determines direction</li>
<li><strong>Volume ratio</strong> — current volume / trailing average volume measures conviction</li>
<li><strong>Flow magnitude</strong> — <code>volume × price × direction × 0.1</code> provides a rough dollar estimate</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">This is an approximation, not a substitute for official flow data, but it captures the direction and relative magnitude correctly. Results are cached for 15 minutes.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Architecture Principles</h2><a id="user-content-architecture-principles" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Architecture Principles" href="#architecture-principles"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<markdown-accessiblity-table data-catalyst=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Principle</th>
<th>Implementation</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Speed over perfection</strong></td>
<td>Keyword classifier is instant; LLM refines asynchronously. Users never wait.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Assume failure</strong></td>
<td>Per-feed circuit breakers with 5-minute cooldowns. AI fallback chain: Ollama (local) → Groq → OpenRouter → browser-side T5. Redis cache failures degrade to in-memory fallback with stale-on-error. Negative caching (5-minute backoff after upstream failures) prevents hammering downed APIs. Every edge function returns stale cached data when upstream APIs are down. <strong>Cache stampede prevention</strong> — <code>cachedFetchJson</code> uses an in-flight promise map to coalesce concurrent cache misses into a single upstream fetch: the first request creates and registers a Promise, all concurrent requests for the same key await that same Promise rather than independently hitting the upstream. Rate-sensitive APIs (Yahoo Finance) use staggered sequential requests with 150ms inter-request delays to avoid 429 throttling. UCDP conflict data uses automatic version discovery (probing multiple API versions in parallel), discovered-version caching (1-hour TTL), and stale-on-error fallback.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Show what you can't see</strong></td>
<td>Intelligence gap tracker explicitly reports data source outages rather than silently hiding them.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Browser-first compute</strong></td>
<td>Analysis (clustering, instability scoring, surge detection) runs client-side — no backend compute dependency for core intelligence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Local-first geolocation</strong></td>
<td>Country detection uses browser-side ray-casting against GeoJSON polygons rather than network reverse-geocoding. Sub-millisecond response, zero API dependency, works offline. Network geocoding is a fallback, not the primary path.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Multi-signal correlation</strong></td>
<td>No single data source is trusted alone. Focal points require convergence across news + military + markets + protests before escalating to critical.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Geopolitical grounding</strong></td>
<td>Hard-coded conflict zones, baseline country risk, and strategic chokepoints prevent statistical noise from generating false alerts in low-data regions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Defense in depth</strong></td>
<td>CORS origin allowlist, domain-allowlisted RSS proxy, server-side API key isolation, token-authenticated desktop sidecar, input sanitization with output encoding, IP rate limiting on AI endpoints.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Cache everything, trust nothing</strong></td>
<td>Three-tier caching (in-memory → Redis → upstream) with versioned cache keys and stale-on-error fallback. Every API response includes <code>X-Cache</code> header for debugging. CDN layer (<code>s-maxage</code>) absorbs repeated requests before they reach edge functions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Bandwidth efficiency</strong></td>
<td>Gzip compression on all relay responses (80% reduction). Content-hash static assets with 1-year immutable cache. Staggered polling intervals prevent synchronized API storms. Animations and polling pause on hidden tabs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Baseline-aware alerting</strong></td>
<td>Trending keyword detection uses rolling 2-hour windows against 7-day baselines with per-term spike multipliers, cooldowns, and source diversity requirements — surfacing genuine surges while suppressing noise.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Contract-first APIs</strong></td>
<td>Every API endpoint starts as a <code>.proto</code> definition with field validation, HTTP annotations, and examples. Code generation produces typed TypeScript clients and servers, eliminating schema drift. Breaking changes are caught automatically at CI time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Run anywhere</strong></td>
<td>Same codebase produces three specialized variants (geopolitical, tech, finance) and deploys to Vercel (web), Railway (relay), Tauri (desktop), and PWA (installable). Desktop sidecar mirrors all cloud API handlers locally. Service worker caches map tiles for offline use while keeping intelligence data always-fresh (NetworkOnly).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Edge Function Architecture</h2><a id="user-content-edge-function-architecture" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Edge Function Architecture" href="#edge-function-architecture"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">World Monitor uses 60+ Vercel Edge Functions as a lightweight API layer, split into two generations. Legacy endpoints in <code>api/*.js</code> each handle a single data source concern — proxying, caching, or transforming external APIs. The newer proto-first endpoints route through a single edge gateway (<code>api/[domain]/v1/[rpc].ts</code>) that dispatches to typed handler implementations generated from Protocol Buffer definitions (see <a href="#proto-first-api-contracts">Proto-First API Contracts</a>). Both generations coexist, with new features built proto-first. This architecture avoids a monolithic backend while keeping API keys server-side:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>RSS Proxy</strong> — domain-allowlisted proxy for 100+ feeds, preventing CORS issues and hiding origin servers. Feeds from domains that block Vercel IPs are automatically routed through the Railway relay.</li>
<li><strong>AI Pipeline</strong> — Groq and OpenRouter edge functions with Redis deduplication, so identical headlines across concurrent users only trigger one LLM call. The classify-event endpoint pauses its queue on 500 errors to avoid wasting API quota.</li>
<li><strong>Data Adapters</strong> — GDELT, ACLED, OpenSky, USGS, NASA FIRMS, FRED, Yahoo Finance, CoinGecko, mempool.space, BIS, WTO, and others each have dedicated edge functions that normalize responses into consistent schemas</li>
<li><strong>Market Intelligence</strong> — macro signals, ETF flows, and stablecoin monitors compute derived analytics server-side (VWAP, SMA, peg deviation, flow estimates) and cache results in Redis</li>
<li><strong>Temporal Baseline</strong> — Welford's algorithm state is persisted in Redis across requests, building statistical baselines without a traditional database</li>
<li><strong>Custom Scrapers</strong> — sources without RSS feeds (FwdStart, GitHub Trending, tech events) are scraped and transformed into RSS-compatible formats</li>
<li><strong>Finance Geo Data</strong> — stock exchanges (92), financial centers (19), central banks (13), and commodity hubs (10) are served as static typed datasets with market caps, GFCI rankings, trading hours, and commodity specializations</li>
<li><strong>BIS Integration</strong> — policy rates, real effective exchange rates, and credit-to-GDP ratios from the Bank for International Settlements, cached with 30-minute TTL</li>
<li><strong>WTO Trade Policy</strong> — trade restrictions, tariff trends, bilateral trade flows, and SPS/TBT barriers from the World Trade Organization</li>
<li><strong>Supply Chain Intelligence</strong> — maritime chokepoint disruption scores (cross-referencing NGA warnings + AIS data), FRED shipping freight indices with spike detection, and critical mineral supply concentration via Herfindahl-Hirschman Index analysis</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">All edge functions include circuit breaker logic and return cached stale data when upstream APIs are unavailable, ensuring the dashboard never shows blank panels.</p>

<p dir="auto"><strong>Why two platforms?</strong> Several upstream APIs (OpenSky Network, CNN RSS, UN News, CISA, IAEA) actively block requests from Vercel's IP ranges. The Railway relay server acts as an alternate origin, handling:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>AIS vessel tracking</strong> — maintains a persistent WebSocket connection to AISStream.io and multiplexes it to all connected browser clients, avoiding per-user connection limits</li>
<li><strong>OpenSky aircraft data</strong> — authenticates via OAuth2 client credentials flow (Vercel IPs get 403'd by OpenSky without auth tokens)</li>
<li><strong>RSS feeds</strong> — proxies feeds from domains that block Vercel IPs, with a separate domain allowlist for security</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">The Vercel edge functions connect to Railway via <code>WS_RELAY_URL</code> (server-side, HTTPS) while browser clients connect via <code>VITE_WS_RELAY_URL</code> (client-side, WSS). This separation keeps the relay URL configurable per deployment without leaking server-side configuration to the browser.</p>
<p dir="auto">All Railway relay responses are gzip-compressed (zlib <code>gzipSync</code>) when the client accepts it and the payload exceeds 1KB, reducing egress by ~80% for JSON and XML responses. The desktop local sidecar now prefers Brotli (<code>br</code>) and falls back to gzip for payloads larger than 1KB, setting <code>Content-Encoding</code> and <code>Vary: Accept-Encoding</code> automatically.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Secret Management</h3><a id="user-content-secret-management" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Secret Management" href="#secret-management"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">API keys are stored in the operating system's credential manager (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager) — never in plaintext config files. All secrets are consolidated into a single JSON vault entry in the keychain, so app startup requires exactly one OS authorization prompt regardless of how many keys are configured.</p>
<p dir="auto">At sidecar launch, the vault is read, parsed, and injected as environment variables. Empty or whitespace-only values are skipped. Secrets can also be updated at runtime without restarting the sidecar: saving a key in the Settings window triggers a <code>POST /api/local-env-update</code> call that hot-patches <code>process.env</code> so handlers pick up the new value immediately.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Verification pipeline</strong> — when you enter a credential in Settings, the app validates it against the actual provider API (Groq → <code>/openai/v1/models</code>, Ollama → <code>/api/tags</code>, FRED → GDP test query, NASA FIRMS → fire data fetch, etc.). Network errors (timeouts, DNS failures, unreachable hosts) are treated as soft passes — the key is saved with a "could not verify" notice rather than blocking. Only explicit 401/403 responses from the provider mark a key as invalid. This prevents transient network issues from locking users out of their own credentials.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Smart re-verification</strong> — when saving settings, the verification pipeline skips keys that haven't been modified since their last successful verification. This prevents unnecessary round-trips to provider APIs when a user changes one key but has 15 others already configured and validated. Only newly entered or modified keys trigger verification requests.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Desktop-specific requirements</strong> — some features require fewer credentials on desktop than on the web. For example, AIS vessel tracking on the web requires both a relay URL and an API key, but the desktop sidecar handles relay connections internally, so only the API key is needed. The settings panel adapts its required-fields display based on the detected platform.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Sidecar Authentication</h3><a id="user-content-sidecar-authentication" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Sidecar Authentication" href="#sidecar-authentication"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">A unique 32-character hex token is generated per app launch using randomized hash state (<code>RandomState</code> from Rust's standard library). The token is:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Injected into the sidecar as <code>LOCAL_API_TOKEN</code></li>
<li>Retrieved by the frontend via the <code>get_local_api_token</code> Tauri command (lazy-loaded on first API request)</li>
<li>Attached as <code>Authorization: Bearer <token></code> to every local request</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">The <code>/api/service-status</code> health check endpoint is exempt from token validation to support monitoring tools.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Dynamic Port Allocation</h3><a id="user-content-dynamic-port-allocation" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Dynamic Port Allocation" href="#dynamic-port-allocation"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The sidecar defaults to port 46123 but handles <code>EADDRINUSE</code> gracefully — if the port is occupied (another World Monitor instance, or any other process), the sidecar binds to port 0 and lets the OS assign an available ephemeral port. The actual bound port is written to a port file (<code>sidecar.port</code> in the logs directory) that the Rust host polls on startup (100ms intervals, 5-second timeout). The frontend discovers the port at runtime via the <code>get_local_api_port</code> IPC command, and <code>getApiBaseUrl()</code> in <code>runtime.ts</code> is the canonical accessor — hardcoding port 46123 in frontend code is prohibited. The CSP <code>connect-src</code> directive uses <code>http://127.0.0.1:*</code> to accommodate any port.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Local RSS Proxy</h3><a id="user-content-local-rss-proxy" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Local RSS Proxy" href="#local-rss-proxy"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The sidecar includes a built-in RSS proxy handler that fetches news feeds directly from source domains, bypassing the cloud RSS proxy entirely. This means the desktop app can load all 150+ RSS feeds without any cloud dependency — the same domain allowlist used by the Vercel edge proxy is enforced locally. Combined with the local API handlers, this enables the desktop app to operate as a fully self-contained intelligence aggregation platform.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Sidecar Resilience</h3><a id="user-content-sidecar-resilience" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Sidecar Resilience" href="#sidecar-resilience"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The sidecar employs multiple resilience patterns to maintain data availability when upstream APIs degrade:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Stale-on-error</strong> — when an upstream API returns a 5xx error or times out, the sidecar serves the last successful response from its in-memory cache rather than propagating the failure. Panels display stale data with a visual "retrying" indicator rather than going blank</li>
<li><strong>Negative caching</strong> — after an upstream failure, the sidecar records a 5-minute negative cache entry to prevent immediately re-hitting the same broken endpoint. Subsequent requests during the cooldown receive the stale response instantly</li>
<li><strong>Staggered requests</strong> — APIs with strict rate limits (Yahoo Finance) use sequential request batching with 150ms inter-request delays instead of <code>Promise.all</code>. This transforms 10 concurrent requests that would trigger HTTP 429 into a staggered sequence that stays under rate limits</li>
<li><strong>In-flight deduplication</strong> — concurrent requests for the same resource (e.g., multiple panels polling the same endpoint) are collapsed into a single upstream fetch. The first request creates a Promise stored in an in-flight map; all concurrent requests await that single Promise</li>
<li><strong>Panel retry indicator</strong> — when a panel's data fetch fails and retries, the Panel base class displays a non-intrusive "Retrying..." indicator so users understand the dashboard is self-healing rather than broken</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Cloud Fallback</h3><a id="user-content-cloud-fallback" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Cloud Fallback" href="#cloud-fallback"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">When a local API handler is missing, throws an error, or returns a 5xx status, the sidecar transparently proxies the request to the cloud deployment. Endpoints that fail are marked as <code>cloudPreferred</code> — subsequent requests skip the local handler and go directly to the cloud until the sidecar is restarted. Origin and Referer headers are stripped before proxying to maintain server-to-server parity.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Observability</h3><a id="user-content-observability" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Observability" href="#observability"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Traffic log</strong> — a ring buffer of the last 200 requests with method, path, status, and duration (ms), accessible via <code>GET /api/local-traffic-log</code></li>
<li><strong>Verbose mode</strong> — togglable via <code>POST /api/local-debug-toggle</code>, persists across sidecar restarts in <code>verbose-mode.json</code></li>
<li><strong>Dual log files</strong> — <code>desktop.log</code> captures Rust-side events (startup, secret injection counts, menu actions), while <code>local-api.log</code> captures Node.js stdout/stderr</li>
<li><strong>IPv4-forced fetch</strong> — the sidecar patches <code>globalThis.fetch</code> to force IPv4 for all outbound requests. Government APIs (NASA FIRMS, EIA, FRED) publish AAAA DNS records but their IPv6 endpoints frequently timeout. The patch uses <code>node:https</code> with <code>family: 4</code> to bypass Happy Eyeballs and avoid cascading ETIMEDOUT failures</li>
<li><strong>DevTools</strong> — <code>Cmd+Alt+I</code> toggles the embedded web inspector</li>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Railway Relay Compression</h3><a id="user-content-railway-relay-compression" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Railway Relay Compression" href="#railway-relay-compression"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">All relay server responses pass through <code>gzipSync</code> when the client accepts gzip and the payload exceeds 1KB. Sidecar API responses prefer Brotli and use gzip fallback with proper <code>Content-Encoding</code>/<code>Vary</code> headers for the same threshold. This applies to OpenSky aircraft JSON, RSS XML feeds, UCDP event data, AIS snapshots, and health checks — reducing wire size by approximately 50–80%.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">In-Flight Request Deduplication</h3><a id="user-content-in-flight-request-deduplication" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: In-Flight Request Deduplication" href="#in-flight-request-deduplication"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">When multiple connected clients poll simultaneously (common with the relay's multi-tenant WebSocket architecture), identical upstream requests are deduplicated at the relay level. The first request for a given resource key (e.g., an RSS feed URL or OpenSky bounding box) creates a Promise stored in an in-flight Map. All concurrent requests for the same key await that single Promise rather than stampeding the upstream API. Subsequent requests are served from cache with an <code>X-Cache: DEDUP</code> header. This prevents scenarios like 53 concurrent RSS cache misses or 5 simultaneous OpenSky requests for the same geographic region — all resolved by a single upstream fetch.</p>

<p dir="auto">Cache keys are versioned (<code>opensky:v2:lamin=...</code>, <code>macro-signals:v2:default</code>) so schema changes don't serve stale formats. Every response includes an <code>X-Cache</code> header (<code>HIT</code>, <code>REDIS-HIT</code>, <code>MISS</code>, <code>REDIS-STALE</code>, <code>REDIS-ERROR-FALLBACK</code>) for debugging.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Shared caching layer</strong> — all sebuf handler implementations share a unified Upstash Redis caching module (<code>_upstash-cache.js</code>) with a consistent API: <code>getCachedOrFetch(cacheKey, ttlSeconds, fetchFn)</code>. This eliminates per-handler caching boilerplate and ensures every RPC endpoint benefits from the three-tier strategy. Cache keys include request-varying parameters (e.g., requested symbols, country codes, bounding boxes) to prevent cache contamination across callers with different inputs. On desktop, the same module runs in the sidecar with an in-memory + persistent file backend when Redis is unavailable.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>In-flight promise deduplication</strong> — the <code>cachedFetchJson</code> function in <code>server/_shared/redis.ts</code> maintains an in-memory <code>Map<string, Promise></code> of active upstream requests. When a cache miss occurs, the first caller's fetch creates and registers a Promise in the map. All concurrent callers for the same cache key await that single Promise rather than independently hitting the upstream API. This eliminates the "thundering herd" problem where multiple edge function instances simultaneously race to refill an expired cache entry — a scenario that previously caused 50+ concurrent upstream requests during the ~15-second refill window for popular endpoints.</p>
<p dir="auto">The AI summarization pipeline adds content-based deduplication: headlines are hashed and checked against Redis before calling Groq, so the same breaking news viewed by 1,000 concurrent users triggers exactly one LLM call.</p>

<tr>
<td><strong>OS keychain storage</strong></td>
<td>Desktop API keys are stored in the operating system's credential manager (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager), never in plaintext files or environment variables on disk.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Bot-aware social previews</strong></td>
<td>The <code>/api/story</code> endpoint detects social crawlers (10+ signatures: Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, Telegram, Discord, Reddit, WhatsApp, Google) and serves OG-tagged HTML with dynamic preview images. Regular browsers receive a 302 redirect to the SPA.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Bot protection middleware</strong></td>
<td>Edge Middleware blocks crawlers and scrapers from all <code>/api/*</code> routes — bot user-agents and requests with short or missing <code>User-Agent</code> headers receive 403. Social preview bots are selectively allowed on <code>/api/story</code> and <code>/api/og-story</code> for Open Graph image generation. Reinforced by <code>robots.txt</code> Disallow rules on API paths.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>No debug endpoints</strong></td>
<td>The <code>api/debug-env.js</code> endpoint returns 404 in production — it exists only as a disabled placeholder.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>SSRF protection</strong></td>
<td>The desktop sidecar's RSS proxy runs two-phase URL validation: protocol allowlist (HTTP/HTTPS only), private IP rejection (all RFC-1918 ranges, link-local, multicast, IPv6-mapped v4), DNS resolution to detect rebinding attacks, and <strong>TOCTOU-safe pinning</strong> — the first resolved IPv4 address is locked for the actual TCP connection, preventing DNS rebinding between check and connect.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>IPC window hardening</strong></td>
<td>All sensitive Tauri IPC commands (keychain access, token retrieval, cache operations, Polymarket bridge) gate on <code>require_trusted_window()</code>. Only windows with labels in the <code>TRUSTED_WINDOWS</code> allowlist (<code>main</code>, <code>settings</code>, <code>live-channels</code>) can invoke these commands — injected iframes or rogue webviews receive an explicit rejection.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>DevTools gating</strong></td>
<td>The developer tools menu item and its <code>Cmd+Alt+I</code> keybinding only compile into the binary when the <code>devtools</code> Cargo feature is enabled. Production builds omit the feature entirely, so DevTools cannot be opened in shipped binaries regardless of UI manipulation.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Error Tracking & Production Hardening</h2><a id="user-content-error-tracking--production-hardening" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Error Tracking & Production Hardening" href="#error-tracking--production-hardening"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Sentry captures unhandled exceptions and promise rejections in production, with environment-aware routing (production on <code>worldmonitor.app</code>, preview on <code>*.vercel.app</code>, disabled on localhost and Tauri desktop).</p>
<p dir="auto">The configuration includes 30+ <code>ignoreErrors</code> patterns that suppress noise from:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Third-party WebView injections</strong> — Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram in-app browsers inject scripts that reference undefined variables (<code>CONFIG</code>, <code>currentInset</code>)</li>
<li><strong>Browser extensions</strong> — Chrome/Firefox extensions that fail <code>importScripts</code> or violate CSP policies</li>
<li><strong>WebGL context loss</strong> — transient GPU crashes in MapLibre/deck.gl that self-recover</li>
<li><strong>iOS Safari quirks</strong> — IndexedDB connection drops on background tab kills, <code>NotAllowedError</code> from autoplay policies</li>
<li><strong>Network transients</strong> — <code>TypeError: Failed to fetch</code>, <code>TypeError: Load failed</code>, <code>TypeError: cancelled</code></li>
<li><strong>MapLibre internal crashes</strong> — null-access in style layers, light, and placement that originate from the map chunk</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">A custom <code>beforeSend</code> hook provides second-stage filtering: it suppresses single-character error messages (minification artifacts), <code>Importing a module script failed</code> errors from browser extensions (identified by <code>chrome-extension:</code> or <code>moz-extension:</code> in the stack trace), and MapLibre internal null-access crashes when the stack trace originates from map chunk files.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Chunk reload guard</strong> — after deployments, users with stale browser tabs may encounter <code>vite:preloadError</code> events when dynamically imported chunks have new content-hash filenames. The guard listens for this event and performs a one-shot page reload, using <code>sessionStorage</code> to prevent infinite reload loops. If the reload succeeds (app initializes fully), the guard flag is cleared. This recovers gracefully from stale-asset 404s without requiring users to manually refresh.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Storage quota management</strong> — when a device's localStorage or IndexedDB quota is exhausted (common on mobile Safari with its 5MB limit), a global <code>_storageQuotaExceeded</code> flag disables all further write attempts across both the persistent cache (IndexedDB + localStorage fallback) and the utility <code>saveToStorage()</code> function. The flag is set on the first <code>DOMException</code> with <code>name === 'QuotaExceededError'</code> or <code>code === 22</code>, and prevents cascading errors from repeated failed writes. Read operations continue normally — cached data remains accessible, only new writes are suppressed.</p>
<p dir="auto">Transactions are sampled at 10% to balance observability with cost. Release tracking (<code>worldmonitor@{version}</code>) enables regression detection across deployments.</p>

<p dir="auto">World Monitor relies on <strong>60+ Vercel Edge Functions</strong> in the <code>api/</code> directory for RSS proxying, data caching, and API key isolation.
